items.body:
World of Sweets is strengthening its Candy Realms sugar confectionery range with a refreshed pack design, new flavour-led varieties and a clear value proposition for convenience and independent retailers.
The updated range has been developed to help retailers offer shoppers affordable, colourful and easy-to-shop treats across a broad choice of popular sugar confectionery. Candy Realms is available in both £1 PMP formats, giving shoppers clear price visibility at fixture, and non-PMP formats for retailers looking for greater pricing flexibility. The range includes £1 PMP bags at 160g and non-PMP bags at higher weights up to 190g. The range also includes a large choice of Vegan bags including Sour Dummies, Fizzy Strawberries and Peach Rings
The refresh builds on Candy Realms’ strong momentum, with the brand reaching £10 million in sales within three years of launch. The range is also home to one of World of Sweets’ best-selling products, Candy Realms Candy Watches & Necklaces, demonstrating its proven appeal with retailers and shoppers.
The new-look packaging has been created to make the range work harder on shelf. Brighter colours, bolder flavour cues, larger product windows and a more consistent brand identity across the fixture give Candy Realms greater stand-out, while helping shoppers quickly identify the product, flavour and value on offer.
The redesign also gives retailers a stronger, more cohesive sugar bag range that can be merchandised together to create a colourful and impactful display. With clear product visibility and improved pack hierarchy, the updated range is designed to support impulse purchase and make shopper decision-making easier in busy confectionery fixtures.
To further refresh the fixture, World of Sweets is adding new Candy Realms varieties, including Pineapple Mix, featuring pineapple rings and fizzy pineapple pieces, and Jelly Faves, a mix of popular jelly sweets including twin cherries, cola bottles and friendship rings.
The wider Candy Realms range includes sour, fizzy, fruity and jelly options, giving retailers a broad and simple sugar bag offer that covers key shopper preferences while maintaining a strong value message.
Nat Panter, brand manager at World of Sweets, said: “Candy Realms has been developed to give retailers a commercial sugar bag range that delivers on value, variety and shelf impact.
“The range gives retailers the flexibility of both £1 PMP bags at 160g and non-PMP bags at higher weights up to 190g. That means retailers can offer clear price reassurance for shoppers through PMP packs, while also having larger non-PMP options where they want more flexibility.
“The redesign is a major step forward for the brand. The packs are brighter, clearer and more consistent, with stronger flavour cues and larger product windows to help the range stand out in busy confectionery fixtures. Combined with new varieties, Candy Realms gives retailers a simple way to refresh their sugar bag offer and drive impulse sales.”
The refreshed Candy Realms range is available through World of Sweets and Hancocks, with new varieties rolling out from Autumn 2026.

items.body:
New research, released today by Asda, finds a third (33%) of the nation admit to having never checked their chests, or having a checking routine. Asda has mapped out the regions with the highest rates of non-chest checking, known as ‘checking deserts’, for a UK-first initiative putting 500 pink trolleys in 10 stores across these regions to increase awareness and stop shoppers in their tracks.
The research found people in the West Midlands (39%) were most likely to say they don’t check regularly, followed by Wales (38%), Scotland (37%), the East Midlands (36%), London (35%) and Yorkshire (31%).
Breast checking awareness remains important nationwide, with 47% of those surveyed keen to keep a closer eye on their own health and 36% wanting to be more aware of potential signs and symptoms. Yet 15% aren’t confident they would know what to do.
The new pink trollies contain chest checking posters as well as a QR code taking shoppers to chest checking guidance and signs and symptoms of breast cancer by charity partners Breast Cancer Now and CoppaFeel!.
The QR code on the trolley handles also takes shoppers straight to Asda’s Pledge-o-Meter; a live tracker of people pledging to check their chests regularly. Taking just seconds, shoppers are encouraged to pledge to check, share it with their friends and family, and choose to make a small donation to Asda Tickled Pink at the same time. Link to the Tickled Pink pledge page can be found here.
The pink trolleys are not the only way that Asda Tickled Pink is encouraging people to check their chests. Tickled Pink products are available across Asda stores this October displaying chest checking messaging, as well as around 900 million till receipts printed by Asda over the course of the year.
“Our Tickled Pink campaign has raised over £100 million in the last 30 years. We are driving awareness of breast cancer and early detection by encouraging everyone to check their chest. Together, we’re putting breast cancer awareness on everyone’s list” says Emma Betts, Charity Partnerships Manager from Asda. “We’re hoping our customers will embrace our bold new pink trolleys and sign our pledge to help us in our mission to get 1,000,000 more customers checking their chest.”
Carrie Green, associate director, philanthropy and partnerships at Breast Cancer Now, said: “The Tickled Pink partnership has achieved amazing things over the last 30 years, but with a third of Brits admitting they’ve never checked their chest, it’s clear more vital awareness work is needed. It’s fantastic to see Asda turning their trolleys pink and sharing guidance on signs and symptoms, whilst encouraging customers to check themselves regularly. The sooner breast cancer is found, the more likely treatment is to be successful, meaning chest checking can save lives.”
Natalie Haskell, CEO at CoppaFeel! said: “These pink trolleys bring a vital reminder directly into communities where people are least likely to be checking, helping to start conversations and making breast awareness part of everyday life. We’re proud to be a part of Asda Tickled Pink to reach people locally with the confidence to know what’s normal for them and act early if something changes.”
Joanna Orford, 59, from Ruislip Manor, who is supporting this year’s Tickled Pink campaign and featured in the Breast Cancer Awareness Month photoshoot, said: “I’m so excited to be supporting Tickled Pink this year and helping raise awareness. I’m very open about my breast cancer experience and the importance of being chest aware.
“After noticing a change in texture in my breast, I went to an appointment with a consultant at the hospital. I was told I had breast cancer. My first thought was my three daughters. I wanted to be strong for them and minimise the impact it would have on their lives. But as treatment progressed, I was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer and knew I needed to tell them.
“After a long stint of treatment, including surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy, I attended Breast Cancer Now’s Moving Forward course, funded by Asda, and it was a safe space for us to share our experiences.
“Chest awareness was vital to getting the treatment I needed, and I want to share this life-saving message with as many people as possible.”
In the 1990s, 70% of women survived breast cancer for 5 or more years. Thanks to the power of research and advances in how the disease is detected, diagnosed and treated, this number is now nearly 90%. Asda Tickled Pink’s funding has fuelled this progress over the last three decades. In total it has raised over £100 million for world-class research, vital education and life-changing support.
Pink trolleys are being rolled out across selected Asda stores in ‘checking deserts’ throughout October, with stores from Llanelli to Colindale championing Breast Cancer Awareness month. Simply pick up a pink trolley and find out more about how you can begin your checking routine.
For more information, images or to speak to a representative from Asda, Breast Cancer Now, CoppaFeel! or hear from one of Asda’s storytellers contact: lauren.candler@smarts.agency

items.title: Shoppers’ healthier lifestyles influencing drink choices but ‘it’s not game over for alcohol’
items.summary: Drink sales increased by 2.9% across Europe’s six biggest grocery markets last year, as shoppers continued to cut back on alcohol but paid more for a new generation of beverages competing for social occasions and catering to healthier lifestyles. Spending on alcohol fell by 0.8%… This story continues at Shoppers’ healthier lifestyles influencing drink choices but ‘it’s not game over for alcohol’ Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Spending on alcohol fell by 0.8% in the UK, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and Spain according to the latest analysis of the FMCG market by Circana, while sales of low- and no-alcohol alternatives grew by 7.3%.
Increased spending on sports, energy and yoghurt-based drinks, as increasingly health-conscious consumers took advantage of a wider range of products, also helped lift non-alcoholic drink sales by 5.4% to €109bn and total beverage sales to €180bn.
Beer, cider, wine and spirits sales were down 0.9%, 1.2%, 1.5% and 2.2% respectively. 43% of shoppers, and half of 25- to 39-year-olds, told Circana they were cutting back on alcohol by buying less, postponing purchases or giving up altogether.
44% said they were buying more bottled water, 31% more juices and smoothies, and 29% more tea and coffee.
Just 15% said they were buying more alcoholic drinks. This is despite heavy discounting, with around 41% of beer and 37% of alcoholic drinks sold on promotion during the year, compared with only 25% of beverages overall.
Speaking following his keynote at the Beverage Forum on 1 October, Ananda Roy, senior vice president of strategic growth insights at Circana, said: “Alcohol has been declining in popularity in the five or six years since the pandemic and this has now led to a wider range of alternatives and healthier products, which give us much more choice about what we drink at home and when we socialise.
“Younger people in particular are drinking much less alcohol and there is no evidence this will change as they get older, as the growing mix of adult soft drinks and lighter alternatives is simply becoming an increasingly normal part of everyday drinking.
“It’s not game over for alcohol manufacturers, but they need to do much more than cut prices and instead look at lighter, lower-sugar and lower-calorie products that can help beer, wine and spirits stay relevant as our drinking habits change.”
Circana also found new beverage products generated an extra €242m in sales last year, including €161m from dairy drinks and €32m each from low- and no-alcohol products and bottled water.
While spending on drinks across Europe rose last year, the amount actually sold increased by just 0.5%, as average price rises of 2.3% also drove much of the sales growth.
UK beverage sales rose by 3.2% to €54bn, accounting for 30% of spending across Europe’s six biggest markets but just 19% of the amount sold.
Some products continued to grow despite higher prices, with the amount of yoghurt-based drinks sold rising by 12.3%, ready-to-drink spirits by 12.9%, and still water and plant-based drinks by 5.2% each.
The picture for the beverage market as a whole improved during the second quarter of 2026, when average prices fell by 0.2% and the amount of beverages sold rose by 1.6%.
Circana’s data found own-label products also now account for 35% of beverage spending, with retailer brands gaining ground in categories including coffee, wine and champagne and dairy drinks.

items.body:
RAW Charging (“RAW”), the leading electric vehicle (EV) chargepoint operator for the hospitality, leisure and retail sectors, is proud to announce a landmark partnership with Sunderland AFC to deliver the largest EV charging hub in the North East as part of the club’s Ready Eco programme.
Highlights
- Largest EV hub in the North East: 20 charging bays (16 x 150kW and 4 x 300kW).
- Powered by 100% renewable energy: reinforcing RAW and SAFC’s commitment to sustainability.
- EcoReady Campaign: Premier League Club becomes one of the most sustainable in the league as part of EcoReady Campaign
- Large investment in the city: RAW has invested approximately £750k into Sunderland.
- Free charging for RAW Rewards customers: Drivers can charge for free following the opening of the hub with RAW Rewards. Free charging will run on Thursday 8 October and Friday 9 October.
Located at the Stadium of Light, the new EV hub will feature 20 ultra rapid charging bays, comprising 16 x 150kW and 4 x 300kW chargers, adding a vital new facility for the community. The hub will ensure a fast, reliable, and efficient charging experience for visitors, fans and the wider community. This initiative is a crucial step in Sunderland AFC’s Ready Eco strategy, which aims to make the club energy-sufficient from renewable sources by 2028 and achieve net zero by 2040.
The hub will be powered by 100% renewable energy, supporting SAFC’s mission to lead on sustainability in sport while aligning with RAW’s commitment to delivering future-proof charging solutions across the UK.
Visitors to Sunderland can take advantage of RAW’s state-of-the-art chargers, which allow for quick battery top-ups in just minutes. The chargers support contactless payments and are compatible with all major EV charging apps. Furthermore, customers can enjoy free charging following the opening of the hub by signing up to RAW Rewards: https://rawcharging.com/rewards. Free charging is only available via the ChargePoint App and not via contactless payment.
RAW is committed to excellence and has been recognised with the prestigious Zapmap Best Destination Network Award for 2026, as well as the ICC Gold accreditation, cementing RAW’s position as the EV charging partner of choice for the UK’s leading leisure, retail, and hospitality destinations.
RAW Charging’s Investment in the North East
RAW Charging is funding, operating, and maintaining the entire charging infrastructure, ensuring seamless access to high-quality EV charging for Sunderland AFC’s supporters and the wider public. The chargers will be branded as part of Ready Eco, further strengthening SAFC’s visibility as a leader in sustainable initiatives.
This partnership marks another major milestone in RAW’s expanding UK-wide network, following recent installations at major leisure and hospitality venues, including Cardigan Fields, Knights Park, XScape Yorkshire and Milton Keynes. By investing in this hub, RAW is making EV charging more accessible, convenient, and reliable for all drivers in the North East.
Jason Simpson, CEO of RAW Charging, said: “We are delighted to be partnering with Sunderland AFC to deliver the largest EV charging hub in the North East. This project is a major new facility for the city and aligns perfectly with our mission to support sustainable travel. By providing ultra-rapid charging powered by 100% renewable energy, we are ensuring that EV drivers have access to reliable and future-proof charging infrastructure.”
Paul Kingsmore, chief operations officer, Sunderland AFC, added: “At Sunderland AFC, we are committed to making a real difference through our Ready Eco programme, and this partnership with RAW Charging is another step towards achieving our sustainability ambitions. By installing a state-of-the-art EV charging hub at the Stadium of Light, we are not only improving the experience for fans and visitors but also supporting the wider transition to cleaner, greener transport in the North East.”

items.title: Boots set to be bought by billionaire Canadian family in fresh blow to London stock market
items.summary: The chemist could be sold for around £6.8billion. Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said a takeover by the Westons would make it 'unlikely that an IPO of Boots would happen any time soon.'
items.body:
Boots set to be bought by billionaire Canadian family in fresh blow to London stock market
Canada's billionaire Weston family is set to buy Boots, abandoning plans for a stock market listing in a fresh blow to the City.
Sycamore Partners, which bought Boots’ US parent Walgreens Boots Alliance last year, could reach a deal as soon as next week with the former Selfridges owner.
A sale could see the British chemist valued at around £6.8billion, according to a report in The Financial Times, dashing hopes of an initial public offering, although no final decisions have been made.
Boots' return after a 19-year absence from the UK stock market would have provided a much-needed vote of confidence for the City.
In June, Australian pharmacists Sigma Healthcare, who had held 'preliminary discussions' with Boots, pulled out of talks, rekindling hopes of a float.
A takeover by the Westons makes it 'unlikely that an IPO of Boots would happen any time soon,' said Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell.
British chemist Boots - which began as a family herbal medicine shop in Nottingham in 1849 - could be bought by the Canadian part of the family behind Primark.
He added: ‘This would be a major blow to the London Stock Exchange which has desperately been trying to attract more companies to float in London. Boots is a major name on the high street and exactly the type of brand that could attract retail investors keen to put money into a name they know well.’
The Weston family would want to make the chemist ‘run more efficiently’ and could invest large sums into improving stores, Coatsworth added.
The Westons are best-known in the UK for the Associated British Foods empire, which contains fashion chain Primark, as well as owning department store Fortnum & Mason.
The Canadian side of the family owns the grocery chain Loblaws and pharmacy chain Shoppers Drug Mart through its Wittington Investments holding company. They sold Selfridges for £4billion in 2022.
Buyout group Sycamore Partners broke up Boots’ former owner Walgreens Boots Alliance in August last year after its £7.4billion takeover of the US group, creating the Boots Group in the process.
It includes the chemist’s UK and Irish chains, Boots Opticians and the No7 Beauty Company. Walgreens Boots Alliance boss, Italian billionaire Stefano Pessina, and his wife, Ornella Barra, continue to own a 44 per cent stake in Boots.
Earlier this year, Pessina, who originally brought together Boots and US chemists Walgreens in 2012, said Sycamore ‘will, of course, have to sell [Boots] sooner or later’.
Former Currys boss Alex Baldock took the reins at Boots, which employs 51,000 staff in Britain, bolstering optimism for a float.
Industry experts have said that Boots has become more alluring to potential buyers and investors as it cashes in on strong beauty sales.
Boots last year saw annual sales rise 3.2 per cent to £7.5billion, boosted by strong demand for its beauty products and weight-loss jabs. The business started as a family herbal medicine shop in Nottingham in 1849.

items.body:
From 1 October, Boots will offer NHS flu vaccinations to all eligible adults, including people aged 65 and over and those aged 18 to 64 with certain long-term health conditions, helping more people protect themselves ahead of winter.
Flu can cause severe illness, particularly in vulnerable groups such as pregnant women, older adults, young children, and those with underlying health conditions. Data from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) highlights the effectiveness of the seasonal jab, showing that flu vaccinations significantly reduced the risk of hospitalisation by up to 40% in adults aged 65 and over during last year’s.
Claire Nevinson, superintendent pharmacist at Boots, said: “Flu can make people feel very unwell and may pose a serious risk to those considered to be vulnerable. As we head into autumns, it’s a good idea to plan ahead and ensure you have your flu jab as early as possible to help protect yourself and those around you from flu and reduce the risk of passing the virus to others this winter.”
Customers can book an appointment at boots.com or speak with their local Boots pharmacist. Those not eligible for an NHS flu vaccination can book an appointment through the Boots Private Winter Flu Jab service.
To help patients make informed decisions about their seasonal healthcare, Nevinson answers five common questions:
- Does the flu jab give you flu? 
“No, the flu vaccination contains a tiny amount of an inactive flu virus that cannot give you the flu. Some people may experience a temporary raised temperature and aching muscles, and you may feel sore at the injection site, but these side effects tend to be mild and only last for a day or so.”
- When should you get the flu vaccination?
“The best time to have a flu jab to ensure maximum protection is in the autumn months before the virus becomes more prevalent. This allows the body to obtain optimum protection. After you’ve received the jab, it usually takes around 10 to 14 days for optimum protection so it’s best to book your vaccination as early as you can.”
- Do you only need a flu vaccination only once in your life?
“No, protection from the flu vaccination declines with time and the types of flu virus in circulation change so the vaccination is updated each year. This is why it’s important to get the flu vaccination every year.”
- Does the flu vaccination have side effects?
“Yes, like any vaccination, it is normal to experience mild side effects after receiving a flu vaccination. These side effects are a result of your body’s natural immune response as it builds protection against the flu virus. The most common side effects, such as a sore arm, fever or fatigue are generally mild and tend to resolve within one to two days. To help your body recover and ease any discomfort, you can consider taking paracetamol if it’s suitable for you, stay well-hydrated, and ensure you get plenty of rest.”

Ted Baker, the iconic British lifestyle brand celebrated for its distinctive design, character and quintessential British wit, today announced its return to standalone retail in the UK with the opening of Ted Baker Tailored on 2 October.
Located in the heart of London’s financial district, Ted Baker Tailored represents an evolution of the brand’s UK retail presence, building on the menswear heritage on which it was founded.
Rooted in the traditions of British tailoring and reimagined for today, the collection creates complete wardrobes for those who value style and attention to detail. From impeccably cut suiting to elevated everyday essentials, each piece combines timeless quality with contemporary design, crafted with purpose and worn with confidence.
“This opening is an important milestone for Ted Baker in its home market and a reaffirmation of the brand’s British heritage and the enduring relevance of the category where it all began,” said Henry Stupp, president, lifestyle EMEAI at Authentic, the brand’s owner. “We’re building on the qualities that have long distinguished Ted Baker, its approach to tailoring, craftsmanship and distinctly British point of view, while evolving the brand for today’s consumer. London is the natural place to begin, and we see this opening as a defining step in the brand’s next chapter.”
The store brings Ted Baker to life through an immersive retail environment where product, design and storytelling come together. Unexpected details and characterful touches are woven throughout the space, creating a contemporary expression of the wit and personality that have long set Ted Baker apart.
“Having designed and produced Ted Baker suiting for many years, Suit Direct has a deep understanding of the brand and its distinctive approach to British tailoring,” said Tim Murphy, CEO of Suit Direct. “Ted Baker Tailored represents an exciting new chapter in that partnership – bringing together our expertise in craftsmanship, attention to detail and contemporary style in a dedicated retail space. We’re proud to bring this new experience to London and look forward to welcoming customers.”
The opening of Ted Baker Tailored marks the next phase of the brand’s UK retail strategy, building on its existing presence as Ted Baker continues to strengthen its physical footprint in its home market.
Ted Baker Tailored will officially open on 2 October 2026 at 12 noon at 155 Fenchurch Street, London, EC3M 6AL

items.title: Early preparation key to smooth DRS rollout for retailers, says RVM maker
items.summary: With just 12 months to go until the UK’s deposit return scheme (DRS) goes live, the decisions retailers make now will shape how effectively deposit return works for their stores. Tomra, the global reverse vending machine (RVM) manufacturer, says the countdown is on and retailers… This story continues at Early preparation key to smooth DRS rollout for retailers, says RVM maker Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Tomra, the global reverse vending machine (RVM) manufacturer, says the countdown is on and retailers now have an important window to turn their plans into practical next steps.
From 1 October 2027, consumers will pay a refundable deposit when buying eligible single-use drinks containers and receive it back when the empty containers are returned for recycling. Retailers across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland selling drinks included in the scheme will have new responsibilities, including charging a refundable deposit on eligible drinks bottles and cans and operating return points unless an exemption applies.
“The businesses that act now will be best placed for a smooth transition when the scheme comes into effect,” says Sondre Henningsgård, managing director for Tomra Collection UK.
“This is an important opportunity for retailers to become deposit return ready. Over the next year, attention will increasingly turn to the practical aspects of implementation – staff training, customer communications, deciding on return point locations and establishing operational processes.
“Retailers don’t need to have every answer today, but having a clear plan in place will make the transition significantly easier.”
Henningsgård says it’s clear from recent discussions with retailers that many are developing their understanding of the DRS scheme and beginning to plan how it will work for their stores, operations and customers.
“Right now, stores of all sizes are weighing up the right solutions and balancing those with how to make best use of valuable space, estimating what sort of volume their returns will be, deciding between manual and automated take-back and looking at how they integrate these plans with their current operations.
“Retailers need time to assess their options carefully and make the right long-term investment. With one year to go, now is the time to define what success looks like for their business and to start preparing for DRS.
“Retailers should look beyond machine size and upfront price and consider the full operation, including capacity, reliability, customer experience and service support.
“A reverse vending machine will become part of everyday store operations for many years, so retailers are not simply choosing a machine, they are choosing the partner they will rely on to keep deposit return running.”

items.body:
Retail boardrooms have spent a decade debating the same question: how many stores do we actually need, and what are they for? While that debate rumbles on, one consumer category has already lived through the entire cycle, from counter service to app-first, and come out the other side with a settled answer.
The British betting industry digitised earlier, faster and more completely than almost any other high-street business, and the way its operators handled the transition holds practical lessons for retailers weighing their own channel mix.
A sector that digitised first
The numbers tell the story plainly. According to the Gambling Commission’s industry statistics for April 2025 to March 2026, the sector generated £17.5 billion in gross gambling yield, up 4.4% year-on-year. Within that, the remote casino, betting and bingo segment produced £8.3 billion, growing at 6.9%, while all land-based sectors combined managed £4.9 billion and growth of just 1.1 %. Online is now both the larger channel and the source of virtually all the growth.
The physical estate has adjusted accordingly. Great Britain counted 8,423 betting shops in September 2018, on the Commission’s own figures. The latest count is 5,617, down 3.6% in a year and roughly a third in under a decade. Total licensed gambling premises now stand at 8,081. That is not a collapse; it is a managed contraction, and the distinction matters.
The retail parallel
Retail is traveling the same road at a gentler gradient. ONS figures put internet sales at more than a quarter of total UK retail sales, and high-street footfall has continued to fall year on year through 2026, according to BRC-Sensormatic data. The strategic question facing a fashion chain or a grocer in 2026 is the one betting operators faced in the mid-2010s: when the till migrates to the phone, what is the shop for?
The betting industry’s answer was not “nothing”. The operators that navigated the shift best did not simply race to close premises; they rebuilt the estate around a different job description, the same omnichannel logic that retail’s own strategists now advocate: the shop as brand presence, service point and acquisition channel, with the app as the engine of range and revenue.
The operator that kept its shops
A useful case study comes from outside Britain. Hollywoodbets, a South African operator that entered the UK market in 2019 and holds a Gambling Commission license for its British arm, opened its first betting branch in Durban in 2000 and grew into a household name at home through physical shops, around 84 of which still trade across South Africa’s provinces.
What changed is where the growth sits. The company still operates its retail branches, but the engine is now its digital estate, where product ranges, from sports markets to the online slots lobby on its international platform, expand at a pace no counter service could match. A shop has finite counter space and opening hours; a digital lobby adds products the way an e-commerce site adds SKUs. The physical branches did not disappear when that became true. Their role changed: local visibility, cash customers, and a brand anchor in communities where the company built its name.
What transfers to retail
Three lessons from betting’s migration travel well beyond it.
Treat footfall as marketing, not just revenue. Betting shops stopped being judged purely on over-the-counter takings long ago; they earn their keep partly as brand presence. Retailers doing the same arithmetic often find a store’s contribution to local online sales changes the closure calculus.
Let the digital channel carry the range. The physical estate holds the edited, high-conviction offer; the long tail lives online, where shelf space is free. Betting operators learned this early because their product count exploded online while shop counters stayed the same size.
Build the loyalty loop across both. The most valuable customer is the one who uses both channels. McKinsey’s omnichannel research found omnichannel customers purchase up to 70 percent more often than their offline-only peers, which is precisely the behavior a well-run cross-channel estate is designed to produce.
The caveats that keep it honest
Not everything transfers. Betting is a tightly regulated category, and part of its shop decline reflects regulation as much as consumer preference, a pressure most retailers do not face. And the products themselves are not comparable to a basket of groceries: gambling is adult entertainment with real financial risk, which is why its digital growth has been accompanied by ever-stricter player-protection rules rather than pure growth-hacking.
But as a preview of where a channel shift ends up, the sector is hard to beat: a smaller, repurposed physical estate; a digital channel carrying the range and the growth; and the winners being the operators who treated the two as one business rather than rivals. The high street’s future may look more like that than either the doomsayers or the store-forever romantics expect.
Gambling products referenced in this article are for adults aged 18 and over. Anyone concerned about gambling can contact GamCare’s National Gambling Helpline on 0808 8020 133, free and confidential, 24 hours a day.

items.body:
Crafted to deliver a multi-sensorial taste journey, Ferrero Collection Experience brings together four flavours across a single box, each built on a delicate, crispy wafer shell and finished with its own coating and decoration.
The range is now available in Tesco and Sainsbury’s stores, rolling out across further grocery retailers in September.
THE RANGE
Ferrero Collection Experience 20 pieces
Ferrero Collection Experience features a selection of premium, unwrapped chocolate specialities in four flavours – Cappuccino, Cocoa, Hazelnut and Salted Caramel. Combining exciting flavours and contrasting textures, it offers a multi-sensorial taste experience that is perfect for sharing a refined chocolate discovery together.
THE FOUR FLAVOURS
Each box contains 20 chocolates across four flavours:
- Cappuccino – A silky swirl of milky coffee filling enclosed in a delicate, crispy wafer shell and a luscious coating. Each piece elegantly crowned in fine dark chocolate.
- Cocoa – A crispy wafer shell, enrobed in fine dark chocolate, embraces a velvety cocoa filling; artfully crafted into an elegantly adorned chocolate delight.
- Hazelnut – An irresistible chocolate speciality: smooth hazelnut filling lies at the heart of a delicate, crispy wafer shell, all wrapped in fine milk chocolate and crowned with an artful swirl.
- Salted Caramel – A crispy wafer and a rich dark chocolate shell surrounds a smooth, salted caramel flavoured filling, elevated by a delicate decoration on top.
Emma Armer, marketing director at Ferrero UK, said: “Ferrero Collection Experience is the next stage in the journey for the Ferrero Collection brand. We’ve created a refined multilayered taste experience, including our signature wafer combined with a delicious smooth filling. With five well-loved flavours including cappuccino and salted caramel, there is something for everyone to enjoy.”
The 20-piece box is available now, with a larger 35-piece box rolling out for Christmas from September/October, featuring five flavours. The collection is completed with an exclusive Almond variant, featuring a crispy wafer shell enrobed in silky white chocolate, a sumptuous almond filling and elegantly finished with delicate milk chocolate drizzles.

St Pierre, one of the UK’s leading premium bakery brands, is expanding into lunchtime occasions with the launch of Soft Pretzel Rolls and Mediterranean Herb Brioche Rolls, two new sandwich carriers designed to help retailers capitalise on changing consumer habits and growing demand for premium lunch solutions. The launch marks St Pierre’s entry into the […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
St Pierre, one of the UK’s leading premium bakery brands, is expanding into lunchtime occasions with the launch of Soft Pretzel Rolls and Mediterranean Herb Brioche Rolls, two new sandwich carriers designed to help retailers capitalise on changing consumer habits and growing demand for premium lunch solutions.
The launch marks St Pierre’s entry into the sandwich roll segment and supports the brand’s ambition to broaden usage beyond traditional burger and hot dog occasions. Lunch is already a significant growth opportunity for the brand, with lunch occasions growing 46% year on year, driven by a 42% increase in in-home lunches. Lunch now accounts for 27% of all St Pierre occasion spend.
The opportunity extends beyond the brand itself. Worldpanel data values the UK lunch occasion at £26.4bn, while consumer behaviour continues to evolve. As shoppers move away from traditional sliced bread, one in five lunchtime sandwiches now features an alternative carrier such as a roll or bun, the highest level recorded in five years. Rolls themselves are also at a five-year high in terms of their share of lunch occasions.
Developed specifically to tap into this trend, the new range gives retailers an opportunity to bring greater variety, premiumisation and differentiation into the sandwich fixture while helping shoppers elevate everyday lunches without compromising on convenience.
St Pierre Soft Pretzel Rolls combine the distinctive flavour of a pretzel with a softer texture and the convenience of a pre-sliced format. Made in France, the rolls offer shoppers a simple way to bring something different to lunchtime.
St Pierre Mediterranean Herb Brioche Rolls pair the brand’s signature soft brioche with aromatic Mediterranean herbs, creating a flavour-led sandwich carrier suitable for a wide variety of hot and cold fillings.
Both products are HFSS compliant, pre-sliced for convenience and available in four-packs. Each roll weighs 67g, with an RRP of £2.50 per pack.
Alison Palmer, head of brand development at St Pierre Groupe, comments: “Lunch represents an exciting growth opportunity for St Pierre and a natural next step in our journey to broaden the occasions where shoppers can enjoy our products.”
“Consumers are increasingly looking beyond traditional sliced bread for formats that offer something a little more interesting, while still being quick and easy to prepare. Our Soft Pretzel Rolls and Mediterranean Herb Brioche Rolls bring premium taste, variety and versatility to the lunchtime occasion, making it easier for shoppers to elevate everyday lunches.”
“For retailers, the launch creates a clear opportunity to drive trade-up, bring greater differentiation and incremental value to the bakery fixture and support category growth, by offering shoppers something genuinely new within a high-value meal occasion.”
St Pierre Soft Pretzel Rolls are available now in 320 Tesco stores, 248 Asda stores and rolling into 320 Sainsbury’s stores from 14 October.
St Pierre Mediterranean Herb Brioche Rolls launched in 254 Asda stores from 14 September.
Both products have an RRP of £2.50 for a four-pack.

items.title: More than 850 retailers get behind Home News Delivery (HND) Month 2026
items.summary: Home News Delivery (HND) Month 2026 gets underway today (1 October), with exclusive customer offers and more than £10,000 worth of prizes up for grabs throughout the month. Now in its fourth year, the industry-wide campaign, facilitated by the Fed, will run throughout October, celebrating… This story continues at More than 850 retailers get behind Home News Delivery (HND) Month 2026 Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Now in its fourth year, the industry-wide campaign, facilitated by the Fed, will run throughout October, celebrating the vital community service provided by news retailers and their delivery teams while helping stores attract new customers and grow their home delivery rounds.
A total of 858 retailers have registered for this year’s campaign, with strong support also coming from across the newspaper and magazine industry.
Customers will be able to take advantage of a range of HND subscription offers throughout the month.
These include six issues of the Financial Times for £15; six months half price from Reach, the Daily Mail and i Paper; a seven-day Telegraph print subscription for £78 or weekend subscription for £34.74; and savings of up to 68% on the Guardian and the Observer.
Magazine publishers Frontline and Marketforce are also supporting HND Month, with 12 magazine titles participating, extending the campaign beyond newspapers and giving customers the opportunity to receive their first magazine issue free through HND.
Participating retailers will have plenty of opportunities to benefit too, with more than £10,000 worth of prizes available during October.
At the heart of the activity is the return of the £200 Daily Prize Draw, with one registered retailer selected every day throughout the month.
Winners will be announced at 10am each day on the HND Month website and will have three days to claim their prize. Once verified, winnings will be credited directly through the retailer’s wholesale news account.
Fed national president Hemanshu Patel said the campaign was an opportunity to recognise the work of retailers and delivery teams while encouraging more customers to experience the convenience of having newspapers and magazines delivered directly to their homes.
He said: “HND Month shines a spotlight on the tireless efforts of retailers and delivery teams, and the valuable community service they provide every day. It also presents a great opportunity for retailers to attract new customers and grow their home delivery business.
“Home news delivery remains a vital backbone for many retailers and for the wider industry. The support we’ve received from publishers and wholesalers has been extremely encouraging, demonstrating what can be achieved when we work together for everyone’s benefit.
“To all retailers, thank you for your continued hard work and for participating in HND Month. I wish you every success throughout the campaign and hope you enjoy a very successful month.”
Throughout October, participating retailers are being encouraged to actively promote the customer offers, make the most of the campaign material available and use HND Month as an opportunity to showcase their delivery service to potential new customers.
The Fed is also asking retailers to share photographs of their displays and stories about their delivery rounds so their work can be celebrated throughout the campaign.
Retailers taking part should check the HND Month website every day during October for prize draw winners, competitions, giveaways, campaign updates and retailer stories.

Built around the instinctive phrase ‘But first, tea’, the campaign celebrates the moments when people choose tea before taking on what comes next. items.body:
Twinings has launched But First, Tea, a major new long-term brand campaign designed to reposition tea’s role in modern life and make it a more active wellbeing choice.
Built around the instinctive phrase ‘But first, tea’, the campaign celebrates the moments when people choose tea before taking on what comes next. Heroing the breadth of the Twinings range, from infusions such as Sleep, Glow, Digest and Moment of Calm to the brand’s Sparkling Tea collection, the campaign shows how different blends can support different occasions. In doing so, it reframes tea from a passive comfort into a simple active choice that helps people prepare, reset and reconnect throughout the day.
The launch marks the next chapter in Twinings’ brand evolution. The brand is bringing more new buyers into tea than any other brand, has helped rejuvenate the category by recruiting younger consumers and with more under 35s buying Twinings than any other brand.
But First, Tea builds on that momentum, with a strategic ambition to unlock new consumers, create new tea drinking occasions and drive further category growth by making tea – and Twinings – an even more active part of modern wellbeing.
The platform follows Twinings’ summer GenTea campaign, which explored tea’s evolving role among younger consumers, finding that almost half of Gen Z turn to tea rather than alcohol as their new ‘Dutch courage’. But First, Tea takes that insight further, presenting tea as a drink that helps people feel ready for the day, the unexpected and the moments that matter.
One of Twinings’ most significant marketing investments
But First, Tea is supported by one of Twinings’ most significant marketing investments, with launch activity spanning TV, outdoor media, paid social, creator content, retail media and shopper activation. The integrated platform brings one distinctive idea to life across every touchpoint, building recognition and relevance wherever consumers consider reaching for tea.
The media strategy brings the campaign’s central idea – owning ‘the moment before the moment’ – to life by placing Twinings at the start of experiences people look forward to. Activity includes premium BVOD (Broadcaster Video on Demand) around entertainment, drama and sport; host-read integrations on Davina McCall’s Begin Again podcast; and playful out-of-home creative tailored to different moments throughout the day.
The integrated campaign was developed with Starcom as strategic media partner and Leo Burnett leading the final creative execution. Publicis Commerce developed the retail activation strategy, while MHP Group, Splendid Communications and Whalar supported across earned, social and creator activity. System1 provided the testing and insight throughout creative development, providing valuable insights to shape and strengthen its effectiveness.
Bringing the platform into product experience
Twinings also refreshed premium packaging across its Green Tea and Infusions range, introducing individual string and tag teabags with notes inspired by everyday tea rituals. The detail extends the campaign idea into the product experience, connecting the advertising platform with relatable moments when people reach for a cup of tea.
As part of the OOH launch, Twinings will feature real customer stories selected from more than 12,000 submissions on a billboard in London’s White City for a weekend in October. Capturing moments when people turn to tea for comfort, confidence or a pause, the stories bring the But First, Tea platform to life through real experiences. The creative execution was led by Studio La Plage, the production arm of MHP Group.
Gill Close, marketing director at Twinings UK & Ireland, said: “We believe tea has a key role to play in a world where people are looking for simple, positive ways to invest in their wellbeing. At Twinings, we are already bringing new energy to the category, attracting more and younger consumers who are discovering what tea has to offer, and we want to grow the category even further. But First, Tea is about reminding people of the simple difference tea can make and giving them more reasons to choose it throughout their day.”

ZRO, the UKs first connected surplus food system, officially launches today, giving manufacturers, retailers and brand owners a coordinated way to identify better outcomes for surplus food. Rather than navigating multiple specialist providers independently, ZRO connects expertise, infrastructure and commercial routes across the food hierarchy, assessing each surplus stream individually to identify the highest-value viable […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
ZRO, the UKs first connected surplus food system, officially launches today, giving manufacturers, retailers and brand owners a coordinated way to identify better outcomes for surplus food.
Rather than navigating multiple specialist providers independently, ZRO connects expertise, infrastructure and commercial routes across the food hierarchy, assessing each surplus stream individually to identify the highest-value viable outcome.
ZRO is a new proposition, bringing the full range of surplus food routes together through one connected system for the first time. However, the capability behind it is firmly established. Built on decades of SugaRich Group operational experience, ZRO connects specialist businesses already embedded within food manufacturers’ operations and supply chains. In the UK alone, SugaRich Group operations recovered more than 800,000 tonnes of surplus food in 2025 – giving ZRO proven scale, credibility and capability from the outset.
The approach is already delivering measurable results. In a recent pilot project with a leading UK biscuit manufacturer, applying the ZRO approach increased food-to-food outcomes from 0% to more than 30% within ten months, creating more than £156,000 of additional value from 438 tonnes of surplus material.
As businesses face growing pressure to improve resource efficiency, strengthen supply chain resilience and retain more value from food already produced, ZRO provides a practical framework that prioritises keeping food in the human food chain wherever possible.
One system, five pathways
Until now, businesses have often needed to work with multiple providers to explore different options for surplus food. ZRO connects the expertise, infrastructure and specialist capabilities needed to assess each surplus stream and identify the highest-value viable outcome across five pathways:
- Prevent – using SugaTrak data and insight to identify where surplus arises and help reduce it at source.
- Redistribute – directing suitable surplus food to people through Company Shop Group’s redistribution network.
- Reformulate – turning suitable surplus ingredients into new food products through ZRO Group Ltd.’s food-to-food capability.
- Repurpose – converting suitable former foodstuffs into quality-assured animal feed ingredients through SugaRich and AB Nutrition.
- Recover – using Mobius’ total waste management capability to manage remaining materials responsibly and recover value wherever possible.
The value of ZRO lies not in any single pathway, but in connecting them so that each surplus stream can be directed towards the best viable outcome.
From Sweetdreams to ZRO Group Ltd
The launch marks the next stage in the evolution of a Northumberland business with more than 30 years’ experience creating value from surplus confectionery and food ingredients.
Formerly known as confectionery manufacturer Sweetdreams Ltd, the business became ZRO Group Ltd in June 2026, reflecting its broader role as the UK operating business developing and delivering the ZRO system, commercial proposition, partnerships and proof.
In the UK, ZRO draws on specialist capability across the wider SugaRich Group, including SugaRich, Mobius, AB Nutrition and ZRO Group Ltd, alongside trusted external partners where collaboration adds value.
As part of Ravago, this combines the specialist expertise and agility of the SugaRich Group with the scale, infrastructure and international reach of a global organisation operating in more than 60 countries.
Food stays food
At the heart of ZRO is one simple principle: if something was made to be food, its highest value is to stay food.
Matthew Stephenson, managing director, ZRO Group Ltd, said: “For too long, surplus has been approached as something to manage once the original route to market disappears. We see a much bigger opportunity: to retain as much of the value already created in that food as possible.
“Every surplus stream is different, so there shouldn’t be a predetermined answer. The right outcome might be prevention, redistribution, reformulation, repurposing or recovery. What matters is having the expertise and routes available to make that decision intelligently.
“ZRO connects those capabilities through one system. It gives businesses a simpler way to explore better outcomes while keeping food as food wherever it is safe and viable to do so. That is where we believe the next opportunity for the industry lies – not simply managing surplus more efficiently but rethinking what it can still become.”
Company Shop group brings established redistribution expertise to ZRO
Company Shop Group joins ZRO as its founding redistribution partner, providing established expertise, infrastructure and national scale for surplus suitable for redistribution.
Partnering with the UK’s longest-standing surplus redistributor Company Shop Group, the redistribution pathway ensures that food and drink perfectly fit for human consumption can be sold to communities who need it most. Company Shop Group redistribute over 117 million items of surplus each year to their network of Surplus Supermarkets and social enterprise Community Shop, making them a well-established partner with the scale and infrastructure required to maximise this pathway for businesses within the ZRO system.
Chris Burns, group managing director, Company Shop Group, said: “We are continually looking at ways we provide practical, easy-to-implement solutions for industry as we advance our mission to help create a world where no product needlessly goes to waste. We are thrilled to be the founding redistribution partner in this industry-first partnership, providing a clear route for businesses to redistribute their surplus as well as alternative pathways as part of the ZRO system.”
Alex Keogh, managing director, SugaRich Group, said: “For decades, businesses across the SugaRich Group have helped customers recover value from surplus food in different ways. ZRO brings those capabilities together through a single commercial framework – an important evolution for our business, and in our ambition to lead the industry towards better outcomes for surplus food.”

items.body:
Aldi has been named Multiple Fruit & Veg Retailer of the Year at the 2026 FPC Fresh Awards for a second year running.
The award is determined through a combination of consumer voting, input from across the fresh produce industry and assessment by an expert judging panel using market data and sector expertise.
Whilst it is a blended approach to decide the winner, consumer satisfaction heavily weights the final decision via the public vote, where shoppers were asked to judge retailers on choice, value for money, freshness, quality and customer service.
The award comes as Britain’s biggest discounter continues to invest in quality and value across its range, with £340 million invested so far this year to reduce prices on more than 1,000 products.
The retailer is also strengthening its supplier relationships, with a commitment to source at least half of its British produce through long-term supplier agreements by 2027, giving producers and manufacturers greater confidence to invest in capacity and home-grown production.
Julie Ashfield, chief commercial officer at Aldi UK, said: “This award means so much because it comes from the people who shop with us week in, week out.
“Our suppliers play a huge part in making that possible, and we’re incredibly grateful for their support, particularly during what has been a very challenging year for fresh produce.
“Despite difficult weather conditions, our growers have continued to deliver exceptional quality fruit and vegetables for our customers while working closely with us to maintain the great value we’re known for.
“It’s fantastic recognition of what we and our suppliers work hard to deliver every day: quality fresh produce at prices that work for our customers.”

items.title: Billionaire Weston family closes in on £7bn Boots takeover
items.summary: The Canada arm of the billionaire family behind Primark is inching towards another deal, as it closes in on a £7bn takeover of Boots from its private equity owners. The Westons are in advanced talks to buy the UK pharmacy chain from Sycamore Partners, ending hopes of a potential London IPO. Discussions are ongoing, a [...]
items.body:
Billionaire Weston family closes in on £7bn Boots takeover
The Canada arm of the billionaire family behind Primark is inching towards another deal, as it closes in on a £7bn takeover of Boots from its private equity owners.
The Westons are in advanced talks to buy the UK pharmacy chain from Sycamore Partners, ending hopes of a potential London IPO.
Discussions are ongoing, a person familiar with the matter said, but a deal is expected to be reached as soon as next week, the Wall Street Journal first reported.
The two sides have been in talks regarding a sale over the last few months after Boots was severed from its former parent company, Walgreens Boots Alliance.
An earlier bid from the Weston’s for Boots was rejected after its offer for the high street chain was reduced.
The Weston’s, a Canadian business dynasty, are one of the world’s richest families. The UK arm owns brands including Fortnum & Mason and Primark-owner Associated British Foods.
Battle for Boots
Boots’ future has been thrown into question in recent months. Sycamore weighed up a potential London listing for the pharmacy chain after purchasing it for £18bn last year.
Talks between the two parties over a sale ground to a halt this summer after the conflict in the Middle East and wider economic shocks damaged business confidence.
Sycamore previously held talks with Sigma Healthcare, an Australian pharmacy group, before they pulled out.
Purchasing Boots would mark a return to the UK for the Canadian branch of the family, after they sold department store Selfridges in 2022 for £4bn.
But the pharmacy chain has struggled in recent years, and was forced to close hundreds of UK stores in an attempt to alleviate economic pressures squeezing British high streets.
Sycamore Partners has been contacted for comment. Boots declined to comment.

items.title: Boots owner ‘closing in on sale to Canada’s Weston family for $9bn’
items.summary: Deal would mark return of Canadian family to UK after it sold Selfridges department store for £4bn in 2022 Business live – latest updates The private equity owner of high street pharmacy Boots is reportedly closing in on a deal to sell the business to the Canadian branch of the billionaire Weston family for $9bn (£7bn). Sycamore Partners, which bought the wider Walgreens Boots Alliance for $23.7bn in 2025, is said to be in advanced talks with the Westons, with the Financial Times reporting that a deal could be completed as soon as next week. Continue reading...
items.body:
The private equity owner of high street pharmacy Boots is reportedly closing in on a deal to sell the business to the Canadian branch of the billionaire Weston family for $9bn (£7bn).
Sycamore Partners, which bought the wider Walgreens Boots Alliance for $23.7bn in 2025, is said to be in advanced talks with the Westons, with the Financial Times reporting that a deal could be completed as soon as next week.
If successful, it would mark the return of the Canadian branch of the Weston family to the UK high street, having previously owned Selfridges.
The family later sold the department store chain for £4bn in 2022. The Westons are widely known throughout Canada for owning the grocery store Loblaws and the pharmacy chain Shoppers Drug Mart.
The UK branch of the family, which operates its businesses through a separate investment vehicle, is known for holding a majority stake in Primark through the parent company Associated British Foods.
News of the prospective Weston deal comes months after Sycamore tried and failed to sell Boots to the Australian pharmaceutical group Sigma Healthcare in a deal that would have valued the business at $10bn this summer.
Sycamore has been widely expected to spin off and sell Boots – alongside other parts of the group – after its takeover of the Walgreen Boots Alliance last year. It as has already split the group into five stand-alone companies.
Boots, which was founded in Nottingham in 1849 by John Boot, has changed hands several times in the past 20 years. After a merger with Alliance Unichem in 2006, the combined company was taken over by the private equity firm KKR in 2007, before Walgreens first took a 45% stake in 2012 and then completed a takeover at the end of 2014.
Boots – which has 1,800 stores across the UK – employs about 51,000 people, including about 6,000 at its headquarters in Beeston, three miles south-west of Nottingham.
This summer it reported that revenues had risen 3.2% to £7.5bn in the year to the end of August 2025, with pre-tax profit up by 25% to £337m. It said strong demand for weight loss jabs and beauty products had helped increase its profits.
Boots declined to comment.

items.title: Owner of Bluewater shopping centre to buy Metrocentre in £516m deal
items.summary: The sale process for the mall was launched earlier this year, drawing interest from the likes of Mike Ashley's Frasers Group.
items.body:
Owner of Bluewater shopping centre to buy Gateshead's Metrocentre in £516m deal
The owner of the Bluewater shopping centre in Kent has struck a £516million deal to buy the Metrocentre in Gateshead.
London-listed Landsec, which also owns Liverpool One, told investors it had exchanged contracts to buy 100 per cent of the Metrocentre from Tynehawk Holdings as it expands its retail portfolio.
Tynehawk is the holding firm for a consortium of investors who took control of Metrocentre after previous owner Intu collapsed in 2020.
It launched the sale process earlier this year, drawing interest from the likes of Mike Ashley's Frasers Group.
The FTSE 100 property group will fund the deal through a £500million equity issue, including a retail offer to UK investors, as well as existing debt.
Shares in Landsec fell 1.52 per cent to 615p in early trading.
Metrocentre attracts more than 16million visitors every year, generating retail sales of £650million from 282 stores.
Landsec's takeover deal also includes an adjacent retail park with 15 units.
The owner of Bluewater has struck a deal to buy Metrocentre in Gateshead
The deal is conditional on dissolving a legacy legal entity from Metrocentre's collapsed former owner Intu, a process expected to take place next month, and on consent from bondholders.
Landsec chief executive Mark Allan said: 'Growing our investment in major retail destinations remains our highest conviction call, given the high income yields and attractive income growth on offer for the right assets.
'Our acquisition of Metrocentre represents a rare opportunity to obtain 100% control of a top-10 UK shopping centre.'
The acquisition marks a further shift away from office developments towards retail space for Landsec, having previously announced plans to invest £1billion in major retail assets.
The property company also agreed on terms for a separate acquisition worth about £100million to further consolidate its retail portfolio but gave no further details.
Completion of both deals will see major retail destinations account for 46 per cent of Landsec's annualised rental income.

items.title: High street tax burden ‘costing jobs and pushing up prices’, says BRC
items.summary: Retail and hospitality have the highest effective tax rates of any sector in the UK, leading to fewer jobs for young people, foregone investment, and higher prices for customers, according to new analysis from the British Retail Consortium (BRC). The study compared the taxes and… This story continues at High street tax burden ‘costing jobs and pushing up prices’, says BRC Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The study compared the taxes and profits paid in 11 main sectors of the economy.
It found the two sectors paid a combined £62bn in taxes in 2025/26 through business rates, employer National Insurance Contributions (NICs), VAT, and other government taxes.
Retail and hospitality are two of the nation’s largest employers, providing millions of jobs across every postcode.
They are the largest source of entry-level and flexible jobs, and a gateway to employment and training for those without qualifications or previous experience.
However, the 2024 Budget added billions to their employment costs. As a result, retail lost 122,000 jobs in just two years, while employment in hospitality fell by 93,000 people.
For every £1 of pre-tax profit made by the sector, retailers paid the equivalent of 72p in business taxes, while for hospitality businesses this figure was 82p in the pound: these are the highest rates for any sector, well above the 50p average effective tax rate of all eleven main sectors of the economy, including the 40.5p tax rate of the banking industry. Hospitality and retail’s effective tax rates rose further in 2026/27.
High streets are particularly exposed to the impact of rising business taxes. The presence of retail and hospitality businesses are what keep high streets vibrant and job opportunities available.
Yet they pay a disproportionate level of business rates relative to other industries and together cover almost a third of the total raised by the tax. The consequence is 1 in 7 high street properties across the country lie empty.
Higher taxes leave high street businesses with less money to invest in jobs and local communities and put further upward pressure on prices for shoppers.
With inflation currently at 3.1%, well above the Bank of England’s 2% target, further tax rises risk adding to the cost-of-living pressures facing households.
Ahead of the Budget, the BRC and UKHospitality are calling on the chancellor to put local communities first and reduce the cost burden on these two sectors, including removing high street retail and hospitality businesses from the government’s business rates high-value multiplier.
Doing so, said BRC, will help protect the millions of people working there and support those who would be hit by higher prices if these warnings are ignored.
Helen Dickinson, chief executive at the British Retail Consortium, said: “The chancellor faces a choice: to continue to pile taxes onto our high streets and the millions of households that rely on them, or to give these businesses the breathing space needed to create jobs, deliver growth, and hold down prices.
Millions of people rely on retail jobs across the country, but the overwhelming tax burden puts those people at risk, with over 100,000 jobs lost in the last two years.
“For every £1 of pre-tax profit made by retail, the equivalent of 72p is now paid in business taxes. This punishing tax burden has clear consequences: job losses, shuttered shops, and a missed opportunity to drive growth in every postcode.
“For the benefit of high streets, young people and shoppers everywhere, the chancellor should use the Budget to deliver a clear path to reducing the rates burden, now and in the future.”

items.title: Vaping Products Duty: What retailers need to know | Viewpoint: Dr Marina Murphy
items.summary: The UK vaping industry is undergoing significant regulatory changes, with recent bans on disposable vapes and potentially major changes to display and packaging regulations. Retailers are having to navigate an increasingly complex set of rules, and from today (1 October 2026), things are going to… This story continues at Vaping Products Duty: What retailers need to know | Viewpoint: Dr Marina Murphy Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Retailers are having to navigate an increasingly complex set of rules, and from today (1 October 2026), things are going to get more challenging.
This year’s budget will see the implementation of the Vaping Products Duty, a new duty that needs to be paid on all vaping liquids, alongside related requirements for vaping duty stamps.
Non-compliant retailers could face fines of up to £10,000.
So, what do retailers need to do and how could the changes impact their businesses?
What is happening on 1st October?
The most noticeable change for consumers and retailers will be the introduction of a new duty on vape liquid. This is charged according to the volume of the liquid and is set at £2.20 per 10 ml, equivalent to 22p per ml. This applies to all vaping liquids, whether they contain nicotine or not, with the standard VAT rate of 20% continuing to apply.
Engage with your customers
Retailers should understand how the new duty could affect the price of the products they sell and be prepared to explain the changes to customers. Retailers should explain that this is a government duty and that all responsible retailers will be implementing the same changes and the same price increases.
Know what to look for
The new rules won’t just affect retail prices; there are also important changes to how vaping products must be labelled and sold. The UK Vaping Duty Stamp will be a small rectangular security label measuring 18 mm × 42 mm. It must be attached to the outermost retail packaging and positioned so that opening the product damages either the stamp or the packaging. After 31 December, all stamps must include a digital code that can be scanned for authentication and supply-chain traceability.
Sell-through period
The government has allowed a six-month sell-through period during which retailers may still sell existing stock that was imported or manufactured in the UK prior to 1st October and is therefore not stamped. This sell-through period ends on 31 March 2027. From 1st April 2027, all vaping products must have a valid stamp.
Review existing stock
Retailers should review current stock and calculate how much unstamped stock may need to be sold by the deadline. They should maintain an audit trail of invoices and delivery documents to prove that the products were imported or manufactured before 1st October 2026.
Engage with suppliers
Retailers should engage suppliers to confirm that any stock received after the October deadline will be compliant and have duty-paid stamps. If retailers believe they may have a surplus of stock that they will be unable to sell by the March 2027 deadline, they should discuss the possibility of returning it to their suppliers in exchange for compliant replacement products.
What should retailers do with unstamped stock?
If retailers are unable to exchange stock with their suppliers, they can consider running clearance discounts or bundle deals to clear unstamped stock before the deadline. Any stock not sold by 1 April 2027 cannot legally be sold without a duty stamp, meaning unsold inventory must be returned or responsibly recycled.
Retailers caught selling unstamped products after the grace period could face significant penalties. HMRC can seize non-compliant stock and issue fines of up to £10,000, with penalties increasing for repeat offences. In the most serious cases, businesses could also face criminal investigation, an unlimited fine or imprisonment.
How can I dispose of unsold or unsellable stock?
- Do not bin unsold stock: E-liquids and electronic components cannot go into standard general commercial waste or regular bins.
- Waste contractors: Use licensed waste carriers or specialised electrical recycling providers, such as local recycling centres, to safely handle surplus hardware.
- Work with your suppliers: Arrange a plan with your suppliers for suitable disposal.
- Check official guidelines: Review updates to the GOV.UK Vaping Products Duty guidance for compliance requirements.
Dr Marina Murphy, is head of external affairs UK and scientific affairs at Haypp
