items.body:
Lowe's takes flight and Boots reaches new audiences: last week’s biggest retail technology plays
RTIH rounds up the stand out retail technology deals, launches, deployments and pilots from the past seven days. Including Paul Smith, Sitoo, Tesco, Asda, InPost UK, Aldi UK, Deliveroo, Instacart, Dollar General, Co-op, Lager 157, Amazon, Best Buy Canada, Fanatics, Kingfisher, LeMieux, LolaLiza, and Revolut.
Lowe's
Lowe's has announced the launch of drone delivery, the newest fulfillment method for the US retailer that promises select home improvement items directly to DIY and Pro customers in as fast as 20 minutes.
A pilot is now live at Lowe's store in Matthews, N.C., and adds to same-day fulfillment options for customers, including buy online, pick up in store; curbside pickup and same-day delivery. The launch builds on Wing and DoorDash's existing drone delivery operations in the Charlotte area.
“Our mission is to solve problems and fulfill dreams for the home. To achieve this mission, we're removing friction from home improvement and making it easier for customers to enjoy their home. Any technology we implement is designed to eliminate that friction so our customers can complete their projects quickly," says Seemantini Godbole, Chief Information and AI Officer at Lowe's.
"By piloting drone delivery, we're addressing a real project pain point with an innovative solution that is integrated into the retail journey, giving our hometown customers next-generation fulfillment right when they need it."
Paul Smith
Paul Smith has completed its roll-out of Sitoo’s cloud native unified commerce and PoS platform for fashion and lifestyle retailers across 31 stores in eight countries. In a LinkedIn post, Sitoo said: “A major milestone with an amazing customer!”
It added: “After months of close collaboration, it’s fantastic to see Sitoo now live across all Paul Smith stores and markets - and even more exciting to think about what comes next. A huge thank you to the brilliant teams at Paul Smith and Sitoo who made this milestone possible. We’re incredibly proud of what we’ve achieved together and excited to continue working closely as our partnership grows. Here’s to the next chapter!”
Tesco
Tesco is introducing new virtual try-on technology for the first time, as part of a trial at its Sandhurst Extra store. Powered by AIUTA tech, the experience lets customers virtually try on around 1,500 items of F&F clothing across womenswear and menswear by taking a photo or uploading a photo of themselves onto a digital try-on screen in the clothing department, or selecting a digital model to view clothes in different sizes.
The trial is designed to understand how Tesco can help customers browsing in-store to discover new styles and feel more confident before they buy.
The virtual try-on screen forms part of a wider F&F refresh at Sandhurst Extra, which includes new changing rooms and a dedicated service hub for easier checking out and returns. Customers will also see a larger F&F range in-store and a refreshed look and feel with new signage, updated lighting and a focus on showcasing the F&F range across womenswear, menswear and childrenswear.
Lager 157
Lager 157 has completed a pilot of ClarityRFID's Clarity Store solution, conducted in collaboration between the two teams across three stores: Naestved in Denmark, Nacka in Sweden and Raisio in Finland. This gave Lager 157 real-time, item level visibility into stock, and the results are now shaping plans for a wider roll-out across the retailer's store network.
During the pilot, Lager 157 says it saw stock accuracy reach as high as 98-99.8% and SKU accuracy climb as high as 97% in participating stores, improving the retailer's head office store level data. A full roll-out is planned for 2027.
“The pilot gave us a completely different level of visibility into our stock, down to the individual item,” says Gunnar Palm, Head of Controlling & Business Development at Lager 157. “That's exactly the insight we want as we plan our next stores.”
Aldi UK
From October, Aldi UK will be trialling a new partnership with Deliveroo across eight UK stores, giving customers access to its full grocery range through the on demand delivery firm’s app. Modelled on Aldi’s partnerships with DoorDash, Deliveroo’s parent company, in the United States and Australia, the latter’s riders will pick, pack and deliver orders directly from stores.
The trial is pitched as the only rapid delivery service available from a discount supermarket in the UK.
Customers will be able to order around 2,000 Aldi products, including fresh fruit and vegetables, meat, dairy, bread, household essentials and Specialbuys. They can order on-demand or choose a delivery window that suits them. A nationwide launch is currently planned for early 2027.
Revolut
Revolut is testing out what is pitched as the UK’s first in-store facial recognition checkout system, Pay with Smile. This taps Revolut Register, a new hospitality PoS hardware system, and is being piloted at select Kiss the Hippo cafés.
The future of in-store payments? Or a solution that is at best looking for a problem that doesn’t exist, or at worst yet another example of a big tech company launching an assault on privacy rights in a ruthless pursuit of profits? Answers on a postcard, please, to the usual address…
Once customers are enrolled, Pay with Smile uses facial technology to verify the identity of the user against the selfie ID checks that they completed when first signing up to Revolut to authenticate and process a payment.
Smythson
ESW has announced a partnership with British luxury lifestyle brand, Smythson, to support its international e-commerce growth plans.
Founded in 1887 and known for its leather diaries, notebooks, travel bags and accessories, Smythson has built a customer base across the UK, United States and international markets. ESW will support its US and rest of world e-commerce operations, providing the cross-border commerce infrastructure needed to deliver a seamless customer experience across international markets and support future growth ambitions.
Seb Villien, Digital & Logistics Director at Smythson, says: “As we continue to expand Smythson’s global presence, working with a partner like ESW allows us to reach customers beyond our core markets, while always maintaining our focus on the quality and experience our brand is known for.”
Dollar General
Instacart and Dollar General have announced a new partnership to offer same-day delivery of the latter’s everyday essentials through the former’s app and website. The partnership will launch with a pilot at approximately 7,000 Dollar General and pOpshelf stores in six states in the coming weeks with plans to expand to approximately 20,000 stores across 48 states this autumn.
“Dollar General’s vast footprint and longstanding commitment to affordability make them an important addition to the Instacart Marketplace,” says Ryan Hamburger, Chief Commercial Officer at Instacart. “As we expand this partnership to approximately 20,000 Dollar General and pOpshelf stores, we’ll help provide customers in communities across the country with even greater access to affordable food and everyday essentials, with the convenience of same-day delivery.”
“Our mission is Serving Others, and we continually look for new ways to provide customers with the value and convenience they count on," says Tony Rogers, Senior Vice President and Chief Marketing Officer at Dollar General. "Our partnership with Instacart provides another convenient way for customers to access affordable food, household essentials and other products they need while saving them valuable time."
Boots UK
Boots UK is kicking off a TikTok Shop pilot, in partnership with THG Commerce, involving a curated selection of No7 skincare and beauty products. Further brands and products are set to launch over the coming months.
Paula Bobbett, Chief Digital and Data Officer at Boots, says: “Millions of people are already discovering beauty and skincare products through TikTok and the creators and communities that they trust. This launch gives us an exciting new way to be part of this dynamic experience and help more customers to discover new products and shop those they love in way that feels seamless and relevant to their lives.”
Daniel Callaghan, Business Development Manager at THG Ingenuity, says: “Boots' debut on TikTok Shop is a testament to the growth and development that the platform has seen over the last few years. This forms part of Boots’ wider ambition to create more connected customer experiences and bring beauty content, product discovery and purchase closer together. Through the platform, it aims to reach new audiences, while giving existing customers greater choice and flexibility in how and where they shop. Huge move, and well done to everyone involved.”
Amazon
Amazon customers in the UK now have a new way to pay for their purchases with the launch of instalment options from Affirm. They can select Affirm as their payment method at checkout and apply to get an instant eligibility decision from the company.
0% Pay-in-3 splits the cost of the purchase into three interest free monthly payments, while a longer-term interest bearing (22% representative APR fixed) plan is available for up to 48 months. Both options are available on baskets of at least £50 and come with no late or hidden fees.
Customers can make payments in monthly instalments, which can be paid manually or set up with automatic debits using a bank account or debit card. They can manage their payment plans at any time in the Affirm app or website and make additional payments or pay their full balance at any time with no early repayment penalties.
JD.com
JD.com reports that its first 101HOME store will open on 28th September in Jing’an District Shanghai. Building on the launch of an online flagship store in 2025, this is pitched as a premium lifestyle retail destination that brings together global design, home furnishing solution, smart technology, fashion, renovation services, dining, art and cultural experiences under one roof.
The retailer says that with its global sourcing capabilities, self-operated retail model and omnichannel infrastructure, 101HOME will offer a seamless “shopping upon seeing” experience, allowing consumers to explore new possibilities for their homes and discover the art of everyday living. Spanning approximately 12,000 square metres across four floors, 101HOME is designed to meet the evolving needs of consumers from age 0 to 101, across different life stages, household structures and lifestyles.
It brings together more than 1,000 full category home and lifestyle brands, including over 30 international brands making their China debut and more than 150 domestic and international brands making their JD.com debut. At the heart of 101HOME are 33 “Dream Homes”, designed for different living situation, family structures, lifestyles and interests.
The Shanghai store features spaces created by British designer Kelly Hoppen, and Japanese designers Shuhei Aoyama and Takashi Honma. Chinese designer Wang Heng (Ryan) draws on Song dynasty inspired aesthetics to create a three-generation family home. Consumers can step into fully designed home settings and see how furniture, lighting and furnishings come together, offering inspiration for their own homes.
Best Buy Canada
Best Buy Canada has selected RELEX Solutions to optimise forecasting and replenishment across its retail network. It says it will deploy the company’s tech to improve inventory visibility, automate planning processes, and support omnichannel operations across stores and distribution centres.
Headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia, Best Buy Canada operates more than 300 stores supported by two DCs and manages approximately 2.1 million SKUs.
It was looking for a solution to improve alignment between inventory and customer demand that would support driving greater efficiency across its network. RELEX’s ability to incorporate supply chain constraints into replenishment planning, optimise inventory across channels, support large scale retail operations, and automate key planning processes aligned closely with its goals.
“Accurate planning is essential to meeting customer expectations in a competitive consumer electronics market,” says Christian Trudel, VP Inventory & Merchandising Operations at Best Buy Canada. “RELEX gives us the tools to improve planning efficiency that supports delivering a better experience for our customers across Canada.”
Airbnb
Home sharing platform Airbnb is expanding its grocery delivery service with Instacart across the US and Canada, allowing guests to order through its app ahead of their stays. This builds on a pilot that started in four cities earlier this year.
Guests can place orders up to three weeks before check-in, with $0 delivery fees on orders of $10 or more. The service does not require a separate Instacart account or app, and the listing address is automatically populated. The service will launch in Canada in the coming weeks.
In Phoenix, Arizona, and Orlando, Florida, hosts can also opt to receive grocery orders and stock the refrigerator and pantry before guests arrive.
Airbnb says groceries have been one of its most requested services. “We wanted groceries to feel like a natural part of a stay, not another errand,” says Juan David Borrero, Airbnb’s Global Head of Partnerships and Business Development.
Asda
Asda and InPost have announced a new partnership that will see up to 700 of the latter’s parcel lockers installed across the former’s UK store estate. This will give Asda customers a new way to send, collect and return parcels while they shop, and is pitched as one of InPost’s most significant UK retail partnerships to date.
The lockers will be installed across a mix of Asda superstores, supermarkets and Express locations.
Joseph Sutton, Director - Express, Fuel & Wholesale, says: "Our unmatched mix of services is a key part of what sets Asda apart, and we know customers increasingly value the convenience of being able to tick off multiple tasks in a single trip. We're delighted to be partnering with InPost to bring parcel lockers to up to 700 locations nationwide.
This roll-out gives customers a fast and flexible way to collect and return parcels, seamlessly fitting around their weekly shop and making everyday life a little easier."
Fanatics
Afterpay has been named the preferred buy now, pay later partner of Fanatics, expanding its relationship with the digital sports platform. Eligible shoppers can now use Afterpay’s Pay in 4 and Pay Monthly for products across Fanatics’ network of online stores.
“Being selected as Fanatics’ preferred BNPL partner is a meaningful milestone for us as we continue expanding into high intent shopping categories where flexibility matters,” says Tanuj Parikh, Head of Revenue, Cash App and Afterpay. “Fanatics sits at the centre of sports culture, bringing fans closer to the teams and athletes they love. Together, we’re offering fans more flexible options at checkout while supporting one of the most dynamic commerce ecosystems in sports.”
The moment builds on an existing Afterpay and Fanatics relationship, which included an activation at this summer’s Fanatics Fest event.
“Afterpay gives our customers the flexibility today’s shoppers expect, so fans can support their teams and celebrate the biggest moments in sports,” says Tucker Kain, Fanatics Chief Strategy and Growth Officer.
“This feature allows us to further our mission to relentlessly enhance the fan experience, whether that’s through the personalised discovery Fanatics Ads brings to shopping, the live energy of Fanatics Fest, or the flexibility Afterpay offers at checkout, and make our world class assortment of products available and accessible in more ways than ever before.”
Kingfisher Group
Kingfisher Group, which owns B&Q and Screwfix in the UK and Castorama and Brico Depot in France and other markets, is using AI enabled productivity tools, including Fabric, to accelerate content creation, enhance SEO and improve conversion.
The FTSE 100 home improvement retailer lifted the lid on its AI and other tech initiatives as it raised its profit target despite seeing a heatwave driven drop off in sales at B&Q. It now expects to make a pre-tax profit of between £595 million and £635 million, having previously guided between £565 million and £625 million. Last year, it posted a £560 million profit.
Other highlights from its full year profit guidance and HY26/27 results include: group e-commerce sales reached 22% penetration. Group app sales now account for 29% of e-commerce sales, with app customers spending approximately 14% more than non-app users.
AI driven personalisation increased +16% generating approximately £100 million of sales, showing, Kingfisher claims, the growing value of its data and digital capabilities. Click & Collect sales were up +9% and home delivery sales +15%, supported by store-based fulfilment network and marketplace growth.
Screwfix Sprint (20 min delivery) was up +50% reflecting the growing demand for rapid fulfilment, particularly in Kingfisher’s City stores. Marketplace GMV rose +42% to £372 million, representing 18% of e-commerce sales. There has been investment in platform enhancements including Buybox, which helps customers find the best offer from multiple vendors by balancing price, merchant performance and delivery speed.
B&Q, meanwhile, continued to stump up cash for search and navigation capabilities, supporting improvements in online traffic and conversion. Natural language search is planned for implementation at B&Q in H2. The next phase of digital commerce will also include agent enabled shopping experiences.
Co-op
Digital commerce data specialist eStoreBrands has announced a new partnership with Co-op to launch Co-op Catalyst, an analytics platform for the quick commerce category. The platform gives suppliers direct access to Co-op's own q-commerce data across coop.co.uk and its delivery aggregator partners.
Suppliers can track product performance, search positioning and store level availability, and use the same data as their Co-op category team. Backed by Co-op's footprint of 2,300 convenience stores and its aggregator partnerships, Catalyst is pitched as providing an up-to-date view of the UK's quick commerce convenience market that has not been available to suppliers before.
Francis Nicholas, VP Product Strategy at eStoreBrands, says: "Having worked for brand owners including P&G and Nomad Foods, I know first-hand how valuable retailer insight is, and this is exactly what buying, category and quick commerce teams have been missing. Quick commerce is one of the fastest growing channels in digital retail, and Co-op Catalyst gives suppliers the retailer's own view of it, which site monitoring alone cannot provide. We look forward to helping suppliers make recommendations that benefit Co-op, their business and shoppers alike."
Kate McCrae, Operations and QCommerce Director, Co-op, says: "We're really excited about this partnership. Co-op is the UK's leading convenience store and a pioneer in Quick Commerce, where we now have around 90% reach across the UK. We are really excited about this new partnership and the insights and opportunities it will bring, as sharing deeper data will be instrumental in helping us, our suppliers, and partners serve Co-op members and shoppers. Co-op Catalyst will help unlock this channel, enabling suppliers to apply core Category Management principles to up-to-date data and recommend actions that accelerate growth for both their brands and Co-op."
Catalyst opens to suppliers later in 2026.
Lagardère Travel Retail
Lagardère Travel Retail is leveraging Perfect Corp.’s Skincare Pro with a view to bringing a more personalised and engaging skincare discovery experience to travellers across its beauty retail operations at airports in Prague, Rome Fiumicino and Amsterdam Schiphol.
The deployment will expand to two additional airports by the end of 2026. Powered by AI skin analysis, Skincare Pro assesses 12 key skin concerns, including wrinkles, pores, spots, texture, dark circles, redness, oiliness, moisture, eye bags, radiance, acne and firmness.
“AI powered personalisation is transforming the way consumers discover and shop for beauty, and travel retail is an especially exciting environment for this innovation,” says Alice Chang, Founder and CEO at Perfect Corp. “With Skincare Pro, travellers can receive an intelligent, personalised skincare analysis and product recommendations within minutes, creating a more relevant and engaging beauty experience. We are delighted to partner with Lagardère Travel Retail to bring this technology to travelers across key European airports.”
Following the analysis, shoppers receive personalised recommendations designed to address their specific skin concerns. Those who complete a skin analysis can also receive a discount via QR code.
VILLOID
StrongPoint has signed a contract with VILLOID, a Norwegian online fashion platform for women. This will see it design and install its new Pio facility, created by AutoStore, a warehouse automation solution.
The contract value is approximately NOK 17 million, and the installation is expected to be completed by Q2 2027.
VILLOID is moving its fulfilment centre to a new location, and the new Pio system will be doubled in size as the retailer requires additional capacity to support future growth. When completed the system is expected to be the largest Pio installation in the world.
"Retailers like VILLOID are looking for partners that understand their fulfilment operations, not just automation. That aligns with StrongPoint's focus on customer intimacy, working closely with customers to understand their operations, improve operational outcomes, and act as a partner rather than simply a supplier. We look forward to supporting VILLOID on its expanding automation journey," says Jacob Tverabaak, StrongPoint CEO.
"We have had a very positive experience with AutoStore Pio over several years. World class logistics with same-day delivery has been a key driver of our strong and profitable growth, delivering on customers' expectations of exceptional fulfilment service. StrongPoint will be a valuable partner as we continue our expansion, and with the new, larger Pio system we look forward to the additional capacity as we scale toward our next milestones. The facility will be the largest AutoStore Pio facility in the world," says Jeanette Dyhre Kvisvik, CEO and Founder at VILLOID.
Amazon
An Amazon Just Walk Out technology powered store designed and built by Gallery has opened its doors at Memorial Hermann The Woodlands Medical Centre in the US.
In a LinkedIn post, Garett Buchholz, Sales at Gallery, said: "It was great working alongside all of the parties involved to bring this store to life. Projects like this take a strong partnership, collaboration, and a lot of coordination, and it’s always rewarding to see the finished product open and serving customers."
He added: "What’s especially exciting is seeing more Just Walk Out technology stores come online within the healthcare industry. The continued adoption speaks volumes about the potential use cases for frictionless retail in healthcare environments and the value it can bring to patients, staff, and visitors. Proud of the Gallery team and everyone who helped make this one happen!"
LolaLiza
LolaLiza has opened a new store featuring a custom AI fashion avatar created by Screenix. Displayed on a Samsung spatial screen and brought into the store in conjunction with DOBIT, the avatar aims to showcase LolaLiza’s collections in a fresh and dynamic way.
A spokesperson for Screenix says: “It turns traditional digital signage into dynamic inspirational content that feels completely at home in the physical retail environment. A great example of how technology, content and strong partnerships can create more engaging in-store experiences.”
They add: “A big thank you to LolaLiza for the trust, and to Samsung Display Solutions and DOBIT for the great collaboration. Congratulations to the entire LolaLiza team on the opening. We’re proud to be part of it.”
Snappy Technologies
Snappy Technologies, part of Snappy Group, has unveiled Snappy AI, a new AI powered assistant designed to help retailers understand their business performance, identify opportunities for improvement and make more informed decisions.
This has been built specifically for Snappy Shopper retailers to help them save time and get more value from their store data. Its initial capabilities will include answering questions about sales performance, bestselling products and helping retailers identify trends and opportunities.
Retailers will be able to ask follow up questions and receive tailored, data-based suggestions and complete tasks that would have previously taken hours in a matter of seconds. Snappy AI can also complete operational tasks, including changing store opening hours and updating product prices.
LeMieux
LeMieux has launched ReRide, a new peer-to-peer resale platform launching exclusively within the retailer's Insiders app, designed to bring its community together while giving quality products a longer life.
A spokesperson says: "By keeping well made products in use for longer, we’re helping reduce waste, encourage more conscious purchasing and create a marketplace where great kit continues its journey with another rider. ReRide is also a destination for collectors and long time LeMieux fans. Whether you’re searching for a discontinued colour, replacing a well loved favourite or completing a matching set from a previous season, ReRide makes it easier to discover those harder to find pieces that are no longer available to buy new."
They add: "Most importantly, ReRide has been created for the LeMieux community. It’s a place where riders can connect directly with one another, share trusted products and help fellow equestrians enjoy the quality and performance of LeMieux for years to come."
Tesco
Vontier Corporation reports that Tesco will integrate technologies from Gilbarco Veeder-Root and Invenco with a view to creating a scalable and efficient fuelling solution across the grocery retailer’s petrol stations.
“By leveraging the combined strengths of our market leading businesses, Vontier is proud to deliver integrated solutions designed to best serve the unique needs of our customers,” says Andy Bennett, Group President of Convenience Retail at Vontier. “Today's announcement combines the retail expertise of Tesco with the best in fuelling from Gilbarco Veeder-Root and best in payment from Invenco to create a state-of-the-art solution.”
According to those involved, Gilbarco Veeder-Root’s DOMS PSS 5000 Forecourt Controller and Invenco’s connected outdoor payment terminals will enable fast and compliant transactions at the pump or at the kiosk. The controller provides specialised software that connects Tesco’s PoS and software, providing real-time data on all aspects of the forecourt.

items.body:
Finnish grocery retailer and wholesaler Kesko teams with KNAPP for new supply chain automation solution
Finnish retailing conglomerate, Kesko, is building a new logistics centre in Nurmijärvi, Finland, and has selected KNAPP as its automation partner for the first phase of the project. Kesko is a grocery retailer and wholesaler and its new central warehouse in Nurmijärvi is being built for the company’s foodservice business for the hotel, restaurant and catering (HoReCa) sector. Construction work began at the beginning of 2026.
“We are building an automation solution designed to serve our business for decades to come,” says Pekka Tala, Development Director at Kesko. “That is why it was important for us to find a solution that not only meets today’s needs, but also enables us to develop our operations in the future.”
According to Tala, the fundamentals of logistics automation have remained similar in many respects, but system performance and reliability have advanced considerably. Software also plays a growing role, as automation solutions guide operations more intelligently than before.
Kesko and KNAPP have worked together previously, and a joint planning process reinforced the view that KNAPP’s solution is well aligned with the objectives set for the logistics centre. The single facility must be able to serve different customers and order types efficiently using the same technology platform.
“KNAPP has a strong understanding of what customers need, as well as innovative solutions and insight into how those solutions will develop in the future,” Tala says. “A logistics centre is a multi-year project and a long-term investment, so it is important for us to choose a partner that can look ahead and understand our needs years from now.”
The solution being supplied by KNAPP combines automation with manual logistics processes. It uses the strengths of both operating models where they best support the needs of the business and customer service. The system is designed to adapt to future changes and growing volumes. It includes automated pallet handling, high bay storage solutions, shuttle-based storage and goods to person small item picking.
“We are pleased to implement this project together with Kesko,” says Rudolf Hansl, Vice President, Food Retail Solutions at KNAPP. “The solution is designed to support future growth and creates the foundation for the continuous development of logistics operations. At the same time, this collaboration strengthens our presence in the Finnish market and marks an important step in further expanding our activities in the Nordic grocery retail sector.”
Planning for the automation solution is beginning now, with installation scheduled to begin in 2028, and the logistics centre is expected to go live in phases during 2029–2030.

In his welcome speech, Scott Thompson, Founder and Editor, RTIH, said: “This is the awards’ fifth year as a physical event. We started off with just 30 people at the South Place Hotel not far from here, then moved to London Bridge Hotel, then The Barbican, and last year RIBA’s HQ in the West End.”
“But I’m conscious of the fact that, to quote the legend that is Taylor Swift, You’re only as hot as your last hit, baby. So, this year we’ve moved to our biggest venue yet, and also pulled in our largest number of entries to date and broken attendance records.”

items.body:
Kingfisher embraces AI as Morrisons makes key appointment: last week's most read retail technology articles
Check out our most clicked retail technology articles from last week, including Simbe, Co-op, Tesco, Boots, TikTok Shop, Adobe, Tapestry, Catalyst Brands, Costco Wholesale, Amazon, Tesco, The Entertainer, Søstrene Grene, M&S, Nobody's Child, and the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
Home improvement retailer Kingfisher taps AI tech driven personalisation as it ups profit target
Kingfisher Group, which owns B&Q and Screwfix in the UK and Castorama and Brico Depot in France and other markets, is using AI enabled productivity tools, including Fabric, to accelerate content creation, enhance SEO and improve conversion.
The FTSE 100 home improvement retailer lifted the lid on its AI and other tech initiatives as it raised its profit target despite seeing a heatwave driven drop off in sales at B&Q. It now expects to make a pre-tax profit of between £595 million and £635 million, having previously guided between £565 million and £625 million. Last year, it posted a £560 million profit.
Other highlights from its full year profit guidance and HY26/27 results include: group e-commerce sales reached 22% penetration. Group app sales now account for 29% of e-commerce sales, with app customers spending approximately 14% more than non-app users.
AI driven personalisation increased +16% generating approximately £100 million of sales, showing, Kingfisher claims, the growing value of its data and digital capabilities. Click & Collect sales were up +9% and home delivery sales +15%, supported by store-based fulfilment network and marketplace growth.
Screwfix Sprint (20 min delivery) was up +50% reflecting the growing demand for rapid fulfilment, particularly in Kingfisher’s City stores. Marketplace GMV rose +42% to £372 million, representing 18% of e-commerce sales. There has been investment in platform enhancements including Buybox, which helps customers find the best offer from multiple vendors by balancing price, merchant performance and delivery speed.
B&Q, meanwhile, continued to stump up cash for search and navigation capabilities, supporting improvements in online traffic and conversion. Natural language search is planned for implementation at B&Q in H2. The next phase of digital commerce will also include agent enabled shopping experiences.
UK grocery giant Morrisons names former Kingfisher executive Mohsen Ghasempour as Chief AI Officer
Morrisons has appointed Dr Mohsen Ghasempour as Chief AI Officer, a newly created role that will see him establish a central data science and AI function for the UK grocery retailer. He joins from Kingfisher, where he had served as Chief AI Officer since March 2024 following more than two years as Group AI Director.
He will take overall responsibility for data and AI strategy, with a remit spanning customer growth, colleague empowerment, operational efficiency, manufacturing excellence and commercial excellence. He will report directly to Morrisons CEO Rami Baitiéh when he takes up the role on 1st October.
“Creation of this new role reflects our commitment to ensuring Morrisons is embracing the opportunities in data and AI at pace, with focus and in the right way,” says Baitiéh.
“Mohsen is a recognised expert in the field with hands on experience of unlocking the potential of technology to deliver innovative new solutions that serve customers, empower colleagues and deliver measurable business impact.”
Ghasempour says: “I’m excited about joining Morrisons and building the team that will help the business make effective and responsible use of AI in the years ahead, to deliver real benefits for customers and colleagues.”
Royal Mail inks deal to boost UK out of home network with acquisition of Quadient parcel lockers
Royal Mail has announced the acquisition of Quadient’s UK-based parcel locker network. Around 3,000 lockers will now become part of Royal Mail’s out of home network. The transaction is expected to close by the end of the calendar year. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.
A Royal Mail spokesperson said: “Together with our existing lockers, parcel shops and parcel postboxes, this acquisition will further enhance our out of home network of 30,000 parcel points and strengthen our proposition for customers. This is an exciting step forward in making it even easier for customers to send, collect and return parcels in the way that suits them best, through lockers, shops and other convenient locations.”
The deal strengthens Royal Mail’s position and makes it a major player in a crowded UK parcel lockers market that also includes InPost, Amazon, and YEEP!
Former McDonald's and Compass Group executive Jon Braithwaite connects with Co-op as new Group CDIO
Jon Braithwaite has joined Co-op as Interim Group Chief Digital and Information Officer. His CV includes stints at McDonald’s, Compass Group, and Gala Coral Group. Braithwaite is also an advisory board member at micro-donations specialist Pennies.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “Co-op is a business that combines commercial scale with genuine social purpose, and few organisations are as trusted. Technology sits right at the heart of how we serve member-owners, customers and colleagues. I'm looking forward to working with the brilliant team here and building on the momentum already underway. Exciting times ahead.”
The clock is ticking: there is now just one week left to get your entries in for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
The eighth edition of the RTIH Innovation Awards is now up and running with the deadline for entries being Friday, 2nd October. That’s just one week away, so don’t delay, start working on your submissions today!
The awards, sponsored by 3D Cloud, Business France, and Retail Technology Show 2027, celebrate global tech innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world. Our latest winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC (Prince Consort Rooms) in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Click here for FAQs, categories, and information on our judging panel.
Sign up for an account and submit your entry or entries here.
Boots pilot launching on TikTok Shop in partnership with THG Commerce on 28th September
Boots UK is kicking off a TikTok Shop pilot, in partnership with THG Commerce, involving a curated selection of No7 skincare and beauty products. Further brands and products are set to launch over the coming months.
Paula Bobbett, Chief Digital and Data Officer at Boots, says: “Millions of people are already discovering beauty and skincare products through TikTok and the creators and communities that they trust. This launch gives us an exciting new way to be part of this dynamic experience and help more customers to discover new products and shop those they love in way that feels seamless and relevant to their lives.”
Daniel Callaghan, Business Development Manager at THG Ingenuity, says: “Boots' debut on TikTok Shop is a testament to the growth and development that the platform has seen over the last few years. This forms part of Boots’ wider ambition to create more connected customer experiences and bring beauty content, product discovery and purchase closer together. Through the platform, it aims to reach new audiences, while giving existing customers greater choice and flexibility in how and where they shop. Huge move, and well done to everyone involved.”
Tesco teams with AIUTA to test out virtual try-on technology for F&F clothing in Sandhurst Extra store
Tesco is introducing new virtual try-on technology for the first time, as part of a trial at its Sandhurst Extra store. Powered by AIUTA tech, the experience lets customers virtually try on around 1,500 items of F&F clothing across womenswear and menswear by taking a photo or uploading a photo of themselves onto a digital try-on screen in the clothing department, or selecting a digital model to view clothes in different sizes.
The trial is designed to understand how Tesco can help customers browsing in-store to discover new styles and feel more confident before they buy.
The virtual try-on screen forms part of a wider F&F refresh at Sandhurst Extra, which includes new changing rooms and a dedicated service hub for easier checking out and returns. Customers will also see a larger F&F range in-store and a refreshed look and feel with new signage, updated lighting and a focus on showcasing the F&F range across womenswear, menswear and childrenswear.
Adobe research shows UK consumers increasingly using AI as part of their online shopping journeys
Adobe has released a new report, based on analysis of over ten billion transactions every month, revealing headline UK spending figures from January to August and how online shopping behaviours are shifting thanks to AI.
UK online spending has grown steadily in 2026 - up 3.9% YTD. Spending growth accelerated from early summer onwards, with June the highest spending month of the year so far (£10.6 billion, up 16.9% YoY), primarily caused by Amazon Prime Day occurring in June this year rather than July.
YoY growth in traffic to retail sites from AI sources peaked in August, up 149% YoY and up more than 1,400% compared with October 2024. Conversion rates from AI traffic sources (which, in the UK, overtook those from non-AI traffic for the first time) were 20% higher than non-AI channels in August.
Tally creator Simbe lays claim to largest commercially committed fleet of shelf intelligence technology
Simbe reports that it has surpassed 3,000 autonomous units under contract, which is pitched as the largest commercially committed fleet of shelf intelligence technology (as identified in the company's research).
In the decade since introducing Tally, an inventory robot, Simbe has been shifting from autonomous shelf digitisation to building a broader platform for the physical store.
Today, Simbe combines autonomous robots, computer vision, RFID, handheld and fixed sensing to continuously capture what is happening inside retail locations: from inventory availability and product location to prices, promotions, and merchandising conditions.
“Retailers are increasingly deploying physical intelligence across the enterprise,” says Deborah Weinswig, Founder and CEO at Coresight Research. “Simbe’s 3,000 unit milestone reflects that shift: trusted shelf-level data is becoming foundational to store operations, digital commerce, merchandising and supply chain decisions.”
Highlights include: More than 75 retail banners globally, including BJ’s Wholesale Club, Kroger, and SPAR; The first and only company to earn UL 3300 certification for a robot designed to operate in public; More than 90% of store managers working alongside Tally say the technology makes their jobs better.
All you need is love and connected teams: presenting last week's biggest retail technology plays
Including Tapestry, Catalyst Brands, Costco Wholesale, Amazon, Tesco, Uber Eats, The Entertainer, REWE, Westfield, Søstrene Grene, Kwik Fill, M&S, and Nobody's Child.

items.title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die
items.summary: Aberdeen is launching an ambitious bid to revive its struggling centre. Could it offer lessons for other high streets?
items.body:
The empty building that used to be the home of Marks & Spencer in Aberdeen is one of the first things you see when you arrive off the train and come into the city centre. The sign has gone, though the shape of the lettering can still be made out; the windows are blacked out and the doors boarded up.
This is my hometown. As a teenager, I spent hours on Union Street, its main thoroughfare, nicknamed the Granite Mile after the local silver-grey stone. It was the place to try on all the latest fashions from the likes of Clockhouse and Chelsea Girl.
The street used to be packed with shoppers from across the north-east of Scotland.
Now, it's pockmarked with empty shops.
"I come to Union Street to take a bus somewhere else... there's nothing to shop for nowâ¦ it's horrendous," complains Marie Sim, a lifelong Aberdeen resident.
It's a similar story across the country: High Streets, once bursting with shops, hit first by the rise of out-of-town retail centres and then by online commerce.
But Aberdeen is in the thick of an ambitious turnaround plan. The port city has essentially declared war on its empty shop problem, taking an unusually hands-on approach to filling vacant units and bringing long-neglected upper floors of buildings into use.
On top of that, the council is pouring tens of millions into trying to make the city centre a destination again. Like many other places, it's leaning into the "experience economy", with a new indoor food and drink market and a major redevelopment of the seafront.
High Streets are integral to how we feel about where we live. The sight of vacant shops and graffiti can quickly become a vicious circle, deterring shoppers, discouraging investment and leading to anti-social behaviour.
Politicians of all stripes have been trying for years to breathe new life into town centres - and Andy Burnham, who has made a focus on "place" part of his political identity, is the latest. He argues they should become "symbols of Britain's renaissance".
But can it be achieved? And if they're to survive, do town centres need a fundamental rethink?
'Too much retail space'
One in eight properties on British High Streets are currently vacant, according to Green Street, the property and retail analytics company, a number that's stayed stubbornly high for years.
"If there was a silver bullet, it would have been fired years ago," says Jackie Sadek, a former government adviser on urban regeneration, who has spent nearly four decades working in town centre renewal.
One of the biggest obstacles is fractured ownership. Shops and buildings are often owned by dozens of different landlords, sometimes through offshore companies or complex structures, each with their own interests and priorities. That can slow decision-making and make large-scale regeneration difficult.
But even with empty units that are available, you need to find someone willing to take them on.
Many units are old and need modernising.
The cost of running a High Street business has also risen; employment costs are higher, and there's the burden of business rates.
Firms need customers. Footfall on many High Streets has been in long-term decline as shopping and services move online, and this enormous structural shift has yet to play out fully.
Two-thirds of town centre experts think there is still 20% to 40% too much retail space, according to a survey by retail body Revo and real estate consultancy Lambert Smith Hampton.
Whack-a-mole shop filling
In Aberdeen's boom years of North Sea oil, from the late 1970s through to the early 2010s, it didn't have to work hard to fill its hotels and restaurants and get the cash tills ringing because of the wealth the energy industry brought to the city.
I remember weekends with friends as a teenager, spending whatever cash we had in the fashion chains and shoe shops. Later came the pubs and bar-hopping, and trips to the art deco Capitol Theatre (now office space), where I saw Duran Duran.
But by the end of 2022, Union Street had hit rock bottom. Aberdonians had long deserted the High Street for a shopping centre, which opened in 2009 next to the railway station.
"They'd fallen out of love with their city," says Bob Keiller, head of Our Union Street coalition, a community-led group formed after an emergency summit to reverse the decline.
The first thing it did was listen to what residents wanted, receiving thousands of submissions. Restoring a bit of civic pride and filling empty units became the focus.
It's been a co-ordinated effort, involving letting agents, the council, landlords, businesses and a big team of volunteers, led by Keiller, a former FTSE 100 CEO, who isn't getting paid. He has a map on his office wall, detailing the status of every property, unit by unit, with colour-coded Post-it notes.
They audited the street, tracking down absent landlords, and logging what was empty and why. Volunteers offered to give the empty properties a clean and a lick of paint, to make them more attractive to let. They also spruced up the streets, picking litter, weeding, and painting bins. A small team still goes out once a fortnight.
There's a website where all the available properties are collated; crucially, all of the financial incentives are also listed. These can include council fit-out grants (where a new business gets money to decorate premises), and a two-year discount from business rates.
In 2023, 57 of the 198 units on Union Street were empty. As of today, 33 have been filled, with a further 14 in the process of being let.
But it can feel like a game of whack-a-mole because since the initiative started, another 20 units have become vacant. "The key thing is, we're filling quicker than emptying," Keiller insists.
Keiller's operations director, David McKeith, describes it as putting an arm round the shoulder of those they can help and being a "wasp in the ear" of people who just say no.
At one end of the office, a small, young team produces social media content, linking visitors and residents to a new Our Aberdeen app, showing what the city can offer.
For Keiller, the "small wins" - like tackling graffiti - are needed to help change public perception.
"We've realised the psychology is not to do it once but be prepared to do it two or three times before people that do these things eventually say, 'there's no point in putting it there because somebody's going to paint over it.'"
The upper floor problem
Attention is also turning to the often-forgotten upper floors of buildings along the once-iconic Union Street. In a separate initiative run by the business group Aberdeen Inspired, experts are getting inside those vacant high-up spaces to identify the barriers to bringing them back into use.
Aberdeen sought the help of a High Street troubleshooter, Iain Nicholson, who's worked with dozens of towns and cities through his Vacant Shops Academy.
Out of more than 1,000 empty units he helped audit nationally, on average more than half didn't have a letting agent actively marketing the property. He says some councils don't even know who the landlords are.
Empty shops, he says, won't all be filled by the market alone. Towns and cities need to encourage a broader range of occupiers, from arts and culture to leisure, health and well-being.
He says what's striking about Aberdeen is its joined-up approach, and the fact people "rolled up their sleeves" and overcame differences. "That's not something you can yet say about everywhere."
New markets and widened pavements
Can other places learn from Aberdeen?
Every town and city faces its own mix of challenges.
Nicholson also helped Crewe in Cheshire. As a smaller place than Aberdeen, it is focusing on arts, culture, and community, with a new women's centre opened this month.
And English councils are being encouraged to take a more interventionist role.
They can now force an empty commercial unit that's been vacant for at least a year to be offered to tenants through a High Street Rental Auction, even if the landlord doesn't want to let it.
It's early days but the mere prospect of losing control of a property is delivering some results. Bassetlaw Council in Nottinghamshire, an early adopter of the scheme, says more than 30 shops across the district have been let or are currently under offer as a result of the policy.
But filling empty units is only part of the challenge. The bigger question is what town and city centres are actually for.
Changing habits mean we won't need so many shops. Instead, it's argued, town centres will need more people living and working in them, with new homes and office space alongside services that can't be done online. With an ageing population, for example, bringing NHS health centres into the heart of a town could be a big opportunity.
In Aberdeen, the building that used to house BHS - a department store shuttered in 2016 - is being converted into an entrance plaza for the new food and drink market.
The physical appearance of Union Street is changing too. Like many Victorian shopping thoroughfares, it was built with a wide road (probably to give space to horses and carriages). Now parts of the pavements are being widened to make it a more pleasant place to spend time, though many Aberdonians are weary of the disruption, and of new traffic restrictions.
Money is a big barrier. Aberdeen's new indoor food and drink market is costing Â£40m, funded by the council and the UK Levelling Up Fund. In other places, regeneration schemes can struggle because the cost of redevelopment outweighs the likely financial return, making support from the public sector essential. And the economics are becoming more challenging.
"Higher interest rates, rising costs of construction and other issues are impacting the viability and delivery of new housing and big redevelopment projects," says Steve Norris, a director at Lambert Smith Hampton. He says that big projects usually require cash from both the public and private sectors.
He wants to see "more creative ways of funding".
Part of Burnham's plan is to give local leaders more freedom to invest in town centres and drive regeneration, building on the approach he has championed in Greater Manchester. But bigger projects take years.
Making it easier and cheaper to open and run a High Street business is one of the more immediate solutions being called for, with business rates a particular concern.
Burnham has promised further rates reform. All eyes are on this month's Budget to see how far he will go. All eyes are on this month's Budget to see how far he will go in England. Business rates are devolved in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
The chief executive of Next, Simon Wolfson, argues that the bigger challenge is not business rates, but planning reform.
"The most important thing that the government can do for high streets is let them develop," says Wolfson, who's also a Conservative peer.
Rome 'not built in a day'
Back in Aberdeen, there are some signs of traction.
Lauren Reid and her mother Rose moved their fashion boutique to Union Street in 2024. A council grant helped with the refurbishment after they decided to make the leap.
Can they make the sums add up? "We're getting there," she says.
She feels the same about the future of her street. "I always say Rome wasn't built in a day."
Right now the area feels like a construction site - but another gaping hole will soon be filled. Robert Keane is a local property developer who in 2023 bought the Trinity shopping centre, once home to Debenhams. The space is now set to be re-occupied by a national leisure brand. A notoriously tiring stairway leading to the Trinity from the train station is also being replaced by an escalator.
"We saw a real good opportunity, because it was dying," he says.
He reckons he can make a go of it, cutting the cost of parking and overheads, resetting rents and being more nimble than previous far-flung owners.
It was a bold move given Lambert Smith Hampton suggests that more than one in 10 UK shopping centres is ripe for demolition.
But he's betting the dynamics of Aberdeen are finally changing.
"I think by 2027 it should look and feel like a different city."
That is certainly the hope. Yet walking along Union Street today, past the boarded-up shopfronts and roadworks, it can still feel like a city caught between its past and whatever comes next.

Fears for piers over ‘devastating’ hikes in gambling taxes
Seaside arcades, such as the one in TV’s Gavin & Stacey, often support small coastal economies during the lean winter months
Owners of seaside arcades fear a ‘devastating’ hike in gambling taxes could put them out of business.

But struggling pubs, bingo halls and amusement arcades could be hit by the costlier levies.
Charles Holland, whose family firm runs seven arcades in the south west – including Burnham-on-Sea, home to Britain’s shortest pier – said doubling the tax would be ‘absolutely devastating’.

Seaside arcades, such as the one in TV’s Gavin & Stacey often support small coastal economies during the lean winter months.
Holland said: ‘We operate a responsible, affordable business. We just want to keep the status quo.’

Will appetite for bakery chain Greggs grow on Burnham backing?
When Andy Burnham revealed his favourite item on the Greggs menu was the ‘sausage, bean and cheese thing’, sales of the duly rebranded pastry doubled the next day near the PM’s No10 North HQ in Manchester.
But has the hot summer dulled our appetite for such savoury snacks? Or will Gen Z additions to the menu, such as salads and iced blueberry matcha lattes, fill the gap?
That’s what investors are asking ahead of the FTSE 250 firm’s third-quarter results on Wednesday.
First half-profits beat analysts’ expectations, frustrating short-sellers who were betting on the share price falling. Instead, Greggs shares have risen by a fifth in the past six months to £18.61.
On a roll: Greggs boss Roisin Currie at No10 this year
Full-year sales are now projected to grow to £2.3billion with profits of £193million, against £167 million last year.
But investors will be looking for evidence that chief executive Roisin Currie and her team will achieve or even surpass these estimates with new initiatives.
Smaller ‘Greggs Express’ units are being trialled at petrol forecourts and other travel hubs focusing on greater convenience and speed.
There’s even a branch at Tenerife airport selling the classics, plus a Spanish omelette roll.
Something for the PM to sample on holiday, perhaps.

items.title: Burnham pledges extra £210m towards regenerating boarded-up high streets
items.summary: Funds to help local people turn empty shops, pubs and clubs into community hubs, shared workspaces and cafes The UK government has pledged £210m to regenerate high streets by taking boarded-up shops, pubs and clubs and turning them into shared workspaces, cafes and community hubs. Andy Burnham said the funds would “help put power back into the hands of locals who know their area best” as part of his effort to “restore pride and bring hope back”. Continue reading...
items.body:
The UK government has pledged £210m to regenerate high streets by taking boarded-up shops, pubs and clubs and turning them into shared workspaces, cafes and community hubs.
Andy Burnham said the funds would “help put power back into the hands of locals who know their area best” as part of his effort to “restore pride and bring hope back”.
High streets continue to struggle, despite multiple government attempts at regeneration, after a shift to online shopping and services such as banking and estate agents, as well as higher business costs including taxes, energy and labour.
The cost of living crunch has also prompted people to rein in spending on non-essentials and driven a shift to dining and drinking at home instead of spending on eating out.
Burnham said it was important to find ways of reviving high streets despite the challenges.
“People don’t measure growth by looking at a spreadsheet,” he said. “They measure it by looking at their local high street. Are shops opening or are the shutters down? Does the place feel like it’s moving forward or being left behind?
“The truth is that too many high streets have been left to hollow out, leaving town centres a shell of what they once were. That must change, and today’s funding will help put power back into the hands of locals who know their area best.
“That’s how we restore pride and bring hope back. Not by telling people things are getting better, but by giving them the power to see and feel the difference where they live.”
A new £125m derelict buildings fund will support local councils to revamp vacant shopping centres, disused cinemas and other abandoned buildings into locally needed spaces such as community halls and health centres.
A further £65m will help communities in England rescue and revamp buildings and businesses at risk of closure, such as pubs and clubs.
Another £20m will be equally split between funding co-operative ownership of businesses important to communities such as pubs and clubs and funding council high street rental auctions to fill properties left vacant for a year or more.
The decision directs existing funds already earmarked for high street regeneration towards community-led schemes. It is in addition to the existing £5.8bn pride-in-place programme that is handing 284 deprived communities up to £2m a year for 10 years towards local regeneration projects.
The government is to announce later this year a full high streets strategy aimed at improving town centres across England.
Research by the University of Southampton found people feel high streets have declined more than any other part of their local area over the past decade as household chains, from BHS to Debenhams, have collapsed while shoplifting has increased.
Rose Marley, the chief executive of trade body Co-operatives UK, said the new specialist fund to back the creation of mutuals was “a game changer”.
Labour pledged to double the number of co-operatives in the UK but its figures showed the number rose by just 0.4% last year to 8,005. Amid difficult times in the hospitality sector, co-operative pubs are on the rise – up 48% in the last five years – but they remain a tiny fraction of the industry with just 377 pubs and other hospitality businesses in the UK at present.
However, Marley said: “This funding shows a government that understands how giving power and agency to communities brings positive change and improves lives, with community, business and local government all working together.”

items.title: Co-op expands coffee pod re-cycling
items.summary: Coffee pod recycling points are expanding to more than 200 Co-op stores following what the group says was a successful trial with Podback, the coffee pod recycling service. The expansion has begun with recycling points being installed in Co-op stores in the south-west of England… This story continues at Co-op expands coffee pod re-cycling Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The expansion has begun with recycling points being installed in Co-op stores in the south-west of England and South Wales.
It builds on a 30-store trial launched in November 2025, which included Co-op’s sustainability showcase stores – in places such as Attleborough, Norfolk – which are designed to test and demonstrate new ideas, technologies and solutions that can reduce environmental impact and improve energy efficiency.
The 30-store trial saw more than 500,000 used pods returned.
Podback executive director Rick Hindley said: “This is another very positive step for Podback as we expand our nationwide drop-off network and give more people more ways to recycle coffee pods locally.
“We’re confident that our partnership with Co-op stores in local high streets and communities is going to make a significant positive contribution to our ongoing work to provide simple and convenient ways to recycle coffee pods.”
Scott McHarg, head of sustainability at the Co-op, added: “We’re delighted to see the Podback trial succeed and grow. It provides an easy and convenient way for communities to make small changes to their everyday life that can create a positive and lasting impact for our planet and natural environment.”
Podback accepts plastic and aluminium beverage pods sold by its member brands, which customers can recycle at more than 1,500 drop-off points across the UK.
Plastic and aluminium are recovered and recycled and coffee grounds are turned into biogas and soil improver for agriculture.

items.title: Minister tries to keep growth spirit alive amid bleak outlook
items.summary: A government minister has moved to keep people’s optimism about the UK economy and spending afloat amid fears that interest rate hikes and a difficult Budget could dampen spirits.  Several analysts, such as those at the research company GfK, have recorded a boost in consumer confidence in the months since Andy Burnham became PM. The UK [...]
items.body:
Minister tries to keep growth spirit alive amid bleak outlook
A government minister has moved to keep people’s optimism about the UK economy and spending afloat amid fears that interest rate hikes and a difficult Budget could dampen spirits.
Several analysts, such as those at the research company GfK, have recorded a boost in consumer confidence in the months since Andy Burnham became PM. The UK economy recorded growth of by around one per cent in the first half of the year, defying expectations.
But analysts at AJ Bell have warned that a deterioration in sentiment levels is on the horizon given a less positive outlook on growth for the rest of the year, with energy costs set to spike and mortgages potentially hit by higher interest rates.
Pat McFadden, the work and pensions secretary, attempted to lift spirits as he said the Budget would boost confidence among households and businesses.
He told the Financial Times: “I’ve known John [Healey] for decades. I know he’ll approach this in a really responsible way.
“He will want to say to the country, the business community and the financial world that this is a stable government and Britain is a good place to invest in business and to start and grow a business.”
Consumer confidence jumped to a two-year high in September, it was revealed by GfK on Friday, but analysts fear surging inflation could threaten further gains.
AJ Bell’s Dan Coatsworth said the improvement in survey data could boost Burnham ahead of the Budget.
“The largest gains in September came from improvements to how the public viewed the economy and their personal finances,” Coatsworth said.
“There is a major risk that this positivity disappears in a puff of smoke if the Budget brings tax changes, and if oil prices remain stubbornly high which leads to a higher cost of borrowing, the price of goods and services going up, and everyone feeling the pinch.”
Growth spirits hit by forecast downgrades
One major sign of market pessimism was highlighted by an alteration in economic forecasts by the Wall Street bank Morgan Stanley.
Researchers at the bank edged up interest rate predictions, saying two successive 25 basis point hikes would come in November and February.
The investment bank told clients to expect these hikes to be accompanied by a slowdown in growth at the start of next year.
Bankers Bruna Skarica and Fabio Bassanin said: “While we still think – and with a decent degree of conviction – that any signs of an improvement in the supply in oil and refined products would leave the Bank of England on hold from here, it is challenging to maintain a prolonged hold as a modal call amid the recent Middle East newsflow.”
Professor David Miles, who is one of three top members at the Office for Budget Responsibility, said on Thursday that the public was partly to blame for problems around the size of UK public debt.
He said “one of the great fiscal problems” and an “explanation” for the rise in debt was that the “public have not lowered their expectations about what the state can do for them and the level of public services in line with the reduced resources which come about as a result of productivity having been so bad”.

items.title: Poundland suitors tussle to buy £30m discount retailer
items.summary: Several bidders will table offers for Poundland on Friday, as the owners of the discount retailer seek £30m for the company they bought for just £1.  Multiple suitors are expected to hand their bids to Gordon Brothers, which owns Poundland, as early as Friday, as the US investment firm rushes to complete a deal before [...]
items.body:
Poundland suitors tussle to buy £30m discount retailer
Several bidders will table offers for Poundland on Friday, as the owners of the discount retailer seek £30m for the company they bought for just £1.
Multiple suitors are expected to hand their bids to Gordon Brothers, which owns Poundland, as early as Friday, as the US investment firm rushes to complete a deal before the Christmas trading period.
The bids expected on Friday will cover a “vastly significant portion” of Poundland’s 600 stores, if not the entirety of the business, an industry source told City AM.
Gordon Brothers is demanding £30m for the discount retailer to cover a shareholder loan of that amount which it inherited from Pepco, Poundland’s previous owners. The majority of potential bidders have not raised concerns over funding this loan.
Modella Capital, the private equity firm which snapped up WH Smith’s former high street stores last year, is among the interested parties, it is understood.
The investor renamed its former WH Smith stores to TG Jones but they have been struggling in recent months, prompting Modella to push through a divisive restructuring deal which could close 150 shops.
US private equity firm Fortress, which owns US discount chain Poundstretcher, has also been in talks over submitting a bid, as first reported by the Financial Times.
On Thursday, City AM revealed that Gordon Brothers is considering a separate sale for Poundland’s 70 stores in the Republic of Ireland, which trade under the Dealz brand.
The investment firm had been initially planning to sell Poundland’s UK and Ireland operations together but has seen significant interest in its Irish business.
Poundland turning a corner, say owners
Gordon Brothers is also weighing up a sale to Poundland’s bosses as part of a management buyout (MBO).
Gordon Brothers have appointed advisors Alvarez & Marsal to prepare a list of formal bids by the end of this month, in the hopes of signing a deal before fourth quarter trading begins.
Poundland has faced a difficult period in recent years, which its current owners have blamed on a challenging economic environment and a drastic restructuring.
The firm fell to an £85m pre-tax loss in the year to September, nearly doubling its £45m shortfall in the prior year. The group’s sales slipped 12 per cent to £1.5bn.
The company’s directors blamed its widening loss on “difficult trading conditions” and a “significant programme of restructuring”.
But Poundland said on Friday that its turnaround is gathering momentum. The retailer has seen 3.3 per like-for-like sales growth in the last three months and is on track to beat last year’s earnings by £80m.
Barry Williams, the retailer’s managing director, said: “Thanks to the amazing efforts of our colleagues and suppliers, our return to growth is the clearest signal yet that we’re getting back to be the kind of business that our customers want us to be.
“With the revamp of all our ranges across grocery, general merchandise and clothing complete, we look forward to the Christmas period with real momentum and confidence.”
Gordon Brothers and Alvarez & Marsal declined to comment.

items.body:
Peak holiday season marketing is no longer a single campaign with a single deadline. Search strategy needs time to build visibility, creator content needs a production pipeline and e-commerce operations need to be ready before peak traffic arrives – yet businesses are risking leaving this critical work too late.
Fiverr’s 2026 Holiday Marketing Index, which surveyed 230 top-rated Fiverr freelancers across UGC, search and e-commerce in eight countries, found that more than half (56%) of e-commerce specialists surveyed say businesses are not prepared at all for the holiday season, while 50% of search specialists say businesses underestimate how long effective optimisation takes.
This highlights the growing importance of sequencing specialist work well before the holiday rush, and needs a critical marketing place put in place to reap the full benefits:
- Now: lock in search strategy. Nearly a third (28%) of search specialists recommend beginning this work three to four months before peak season.
- Now through November: invest in creator talent. 87% of UGC creators recommend working with creators one to four months ahead.
- October through December: focus on e-commerce management. 74% of specialists recommend that this work begins one to three months before peak season.
AI is changing the brief, making specialist expertise more valuable
AI is changing how marketing work gets done, but the research suggests it is not replacing human expertise. Instead, clients are bringing freelancers into the process earlier to shape the strategy, not simply execute it. Across UGC (76%), e-commerce (79%) and search (83%), specialists say clients are increasingly hiring them for judgement, advice and expertise, rather than simple execution.
This is creating tension in how marketing expertise is valued. While 93% of e-commerce specialists agree that AI helps them deliver more value to clients, 61% of search specialists say clients expect lower prices simply because AI is involved. Yet 89% say clients ultimately care more about outcomes than whether AI tools have been used.
The shift is particularly visible in content creation as 76% of UGC creators use AI for scripting, 45% use it for ideation and 41% for research. At the same time, 69% report rising holiday demand for UGC, including increased requests for Meta UGC, TikTok UGC and short-form product video. As AI makes content faster to produce, creators are increasingly being asked to help shape work that feels real and relevant.
Abigail G, a UGC creator on Fiverr, comments, “Working across both modelling and UGC, I’ve watched audiences move further away from perfection. First, people pushed back against overly airbrushed advertising; now, with the rise of AI, they’re questioning what’s even real. I think that’s why UGC resonates so strongly: people want real people and content they can actually relate to.”
Discovery, credibility and conversion are converging
Search is also becoming more complex as businesses seek visibility across traditional search and AI-generated answers. Around two-thirds (67%) of those surveyed say requests for generative engine optimisation (GEO) have grown over the past year, ahead of client demand for optimisation for Google rankings (56%). However, 61% still rank Google SEO as the strongest long-term investment, suggesting businesses need to invest in both rather than choose between them. Business demand for GEO services have also increased by 29% on Fiverr’s marketplace over a six-month period from November 2025 to April 2026.
But GEO and SEO are just one step in the journey. Once shoppers arrive, e-commerce specialists report rising demand for the work needed to turn traffic into sales. 57% report increased requests for store management, while 43% report rising demand for both Shopify optimisation and conversion rate optimisation.
“AI alone isn’t enough for any retailer to succeed this holiday season, it takes outside expertise to actually make it work,” said Shiri Hellmann, VP of Global Brand Communications at Fiverr. “Retailers are turning to specialists who know how to get recommended by AI search tools and creators who know how to earn a shopper’s trust. That combination is what’s setting the successful ones apart.”
To help businesses bring creator credibility, e-commerce strategy, and search expertise into one holiday plan, Fiverr is giving 40 businesses $200 for the freelancer services they need to walk into peak season better prepared. Build your business here: https://www.fiverr.com/cp/

items.title: Direct Selling Association renews standards campaign amid growing concerns over AI-generated marketing content

The Direct Selling Association (DSA), the UK trade body for direct-to-consumer (D2C) retail, has renewed its calls for greater adoption of recognised industry standards across the UK market, calling the situation ‘increasingly urgent’. Susannah Schofield OBE, Director General of the Association, which counts D2C retailers Avon, Oriflame, Usborne, and Neal’s Yard Remedies Organics among its members, cited […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
The Direct Selling Association (DSA), the UK trade body for direct-to-consumer (D2C) retail, has renewed its calls for greater adoption of recognised industry standards across the UK market, calling the situation ‘increasingly urgent’.
Susannah Schofield OBE, Director General of the Association, which counts D2C retailers Avon, Oriflame, Usborne, and Neal’s Yard Remedies Organics among its members, cited the rise of artificial intelligence (AI), social commerce and continued demand for flexible earning opportunities to supplement household income, as creating significant new challenges for the sector.
Susannah Schofield OBE, director general of the Direct Selling Association, comments: “The way products are discovered, marketed and purchased has changed dramatically in recent years, and consumers are increasingly engaging with brands through social platforms, while businesses are making greater use of AI-powered tools.
“While AI is creating significant opportunities for legitimate direct-to-consumer businesses, it is also making it easier than ever for rogue players to appear legitimate through the creation of seemingly authentic product descriptions, earnings claims or health-related content that may not be legally compliant. The sheer volume of such material can make it challenging for already-stretched consumer bodies to keep up, increasing the importance of transparency, accountability and consumer trust.”
According to the Chartered Trading Standards Institute, spending on trading standards has been cut by 50% over the past decade1, and staffing levels have fallen by 30%-50% 2.
Schofield OBE continues: “The result is a growing risk of a ‘perfect storm’, making it increasingly urgent for legitimate D2C retailers to demonstrate their commitment to high standards, transparency and consumer protection through recognised industry frameworks.”
Recent complaints investigated by the Association include assisting a UK consumer who had invested more than £15,000 in a business opportunity promoted by an overseas direct selling organisation. Working with international counterparts and the company’s compliance team, the DSA helped secure an investigation that ultimately led to the suspension of the individual involved and a settlement with the complainant.
The Association has also provided support to Trading Standards investigating rogue operators and has supplied evidence relating to industry standards and best practice in a case involving alleged misconduct.
Schofield OBE adds: “Our concerns are not limited to rogue operators entering the market. There remain a number of established businesses operating within the sector that have yet to adopt recognised industry Codes of Conduct.”
Since launching its original campaign in January 2024, the Association has engaged with businesses across the sector, as well as policymakers, regulators and industry stakeholders, and has seen growing awareness of industry standards. However, the emergence of AI-enabled marketing techniques and the rapid growth of social commerce have created fresh challenges that reinforce the need for wider adoption of recognised Codes of Conduct.
The Association believes the demand for flexible earning opportunities is likely to remain strong in the years ahead. However, it warns that as social commerce grows and technology such as AI reduces the barriers to market entry, consumers and independent sellers alike must be able to identify businesses that operate to the highest standards.
As a result, it is urging consumers and prospective independent sellers to look for the Direct Selling Association logo when choosing a direct selling company, providing reassurance that the business has been independently assessed against the industry’s Codes of Conduct.
The Association’s Codes of Conduct, which go above and beyond UK consumer law, offer higher levels of protection to both customers and independent direct sellers, setting out clear requirements covering ethical business practices, transparent marketing, fair treatment of independent sellers, customer protections and effective complaint handling procedures.
Membership of the Association is only granted following a rigorous audit process designed to ensure compliance with these standards. Companies are required to demonstrate that their policies, procedures and business practices meet the Association’s strict requirements before membership is approved, and member companies are regularly monitored and audited to ensure compliance is maintained.
Susannah Schofield OBE concludes: “The direct selling sector has long provided a valuable route to entrepreneurship and flexible earning for hundreds of thousands of people across the UK. As our industry continues to evolve, maintaining public confidence must remain a shared priority.
“Our message is simple: innovation and growth should go hand-in-hand with high standards. We want to see more companies embrace the industry’s Codes of Conduct and demonstrate their commitment to doing business responsibly. That commitment benefits consumers, independent sellers and the wider reputation of the sector as a whole.”
