items.body:
MANGO, an international leader in the world of fashion, has opened its newest store in Chester, creating over 16 new jobs, as it seeks to expand its presence across the north of England.
Situated in Eastgate Square Shopping Centre, the new store offers MANGO’s latest Woman and Man collections, including clothing, footwear and accessories all designed at MANGO’s Barcelona atelier by a time of 500 experts. Combining timeless and versatile staples with more stylish contemporary pieces influenced by the brand’s Mediterranean heritage, MANGO’s Woman and Man collections offer quality fashion at reasonable prices.
The new 6,200sq ft store also reflects MANGO’s New Med concept – an interior design inspired by the brand’s Mediterranean heritage and culture, with natural textures, warm tones and sustainable materials that create a bright and welcoming shopping space.
This latest opening is the second location in Chester and forms part of MANGO’s 2024–2026 4Es Strategic Plan, which aims to drive sales and store expansion. This includes an ambitious roadmap to expand MANGO’s store presence across the UK, a top 10 market for revenue and priority for growth. This year, expansion in the UK is focusing on southern and northern England, with new locations opening in Cheltenham, and Kensington and King’s Road in London, in addition to the Chester site.
The expansion plan builds on MANGO’s strong performance in the first half of 2026, reporting a global turnover of €1.852 billion, up 7.2% year on year (10.7% at constant exchange rates). This growth was driven by the popularity of its collections, including collaborations with Eckhaus Latta and British tailoring house Richard James, alongside continued new store openings.
Fiona Cullen, international regional director for the UK & Ireland, commented: “Our new Woman and Man store in Chester is a confident step forward for MANGO, building on the strong progress we have made over the last year to broaden the appeal of MANGO to even more customers across the UK. Chester is the perfect home to introduce our Woman and Man collections to customers in the north of England, in a store format that truly represents the Mediterranean soul of our brand.”
MANGO has been present in the UK since 1998. At the end of 2025, the company had over 100 points of sale across the UK, including standalone stores and concessions, as well as Mango.com and an online presence across other marketplaces.

items.body:
Tesco is introducing new virtual try-on technology for the first time, as part of a trial at its Sandhurst Extra store. The store will have also have a newly refreshed F&F Clothing service hub designed to give customers more ways to discover the latest styles with confidence.
The new in-store experience will allow customers to virtually try on around 1,500 items of F&F clothing across womenswear and menswear by taking a photo or uploading a photo of themselves onto a digital try-on screen in the clothing department, or selecting a digital model to view clothes in different sizes. The trial is designed to understand how Tesco can help customers browsing in store to discover new styles and feel more confident before they buy.
The virtual try-on screen forms part of a wider F&F refresh at Sandhurst Extra, which includes new changing rooms and a dedicated service hub for easier checking out and returns. Customers will also see a larger F&F range in store and a refreshed look and feel with new signage, updated lighting and a focus on showcasing the F&F range across womenswear, menswear and childrenswear.
The trial comes as Tesco announces the expansion of its online fashion offer, following its successful launch last year. Customers can now shop hundreds of additional styles, more sizes, and online-exclusive ranges, while improved search tools, curated styling inspiration and fashion-led imagery makes it easier than ever for customers to discover and shop the latest collections in the way that suits them best.
Across Home and everyday essentials, work has also taken place to offer new homeware displays and clearer signage. This was based on customer insight into how customers want to shop for the products they need most, aligning F&F Home with the wider F&F clothing brand.
These changes also form part of the wider refurbishment at Sandhurst Extra, with customers also benefitting from a range of improvements across the store, including:
- An improved Food To Go area with a wide range of Meal Deal options.
- A larger Fresh Market section offering fruit and vegetables in an easily accessible location.
- A refreshed Bakery, with a bread slicer for customer use.
- New and improved ranges across homeware, flowers and plants, beers, wines and spirits, Pets, Free From, Health, Beauty & Wellness.
- A new Holland & Barrett shop within a shop.
- New, energy-saving fridges and freezers.
- Refurbishment of lifts and escalators.
- New signage to help customers find what they need easily.

items.title: Prolific Sussex shoplifter tagged to curb offending
items.summary: A prolific shoplifter has become the first offender in West Sussex to be fitted with an electronic tag to prevent further offending. Daryl Hunt, aged 30, has also been banned from entering all Co-op stores in West Sussex. It follows his latest crime spree, where… This story continues at Prolific Sussex shoplifter tagged to curb offending Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Daryl Hunt, aged 30, has also been banned from entering all Co-op stores in West Sussex.
It follows his latest crime spree, where he admitted 13 shoplifting offences at Co-op stores in Worthing.
Hunt, of no fixed address, appeared before Worthing Magistrates’ Court last week.
It followed the offences which took place between November last year and March this year at the Co-op in South Street, Tarring.
Hunt had stolen cheeses, protein bars, washing powder, chocolate, burgers, sea bass and other items.
He received a six-month suspended prison sentence and was ordered to complete six months of mental health treatment and 30 rehabilitation activity sessions.
The court also imposed a three-year Criminal Behaviour Order that bans him from entering Co-op stores.
The order has ordered Hunt to wear a Buddi tag, which provides GPS monitoring of his movements to prevent reoffending.
He has become the first convicted offender in West Sussex to be fitted with the tag on 19 August following a successful pilot of the tags in East Sussex.
Under the Operation Stop pilot, repeat shoplifting offenders are issued with Buddi tags – discreet GPS ankle devices – as part of a Criminal Behaviour Order.
These tags allow police to monitor offenders’ movements in real time, helping to deter further offences, encouraging positive behavioural change, and enabling swift action if breaches or tampering occur.
Inspector Chris Bryant said: “We understand the impact shoplifting has on businesses and the wider community.
“Buddi tags are another tool at our disposal to support businesses and to ensure that prolific offenders are effectively monitored.
“In Sussex, we are leading the way with this innovative scheme to tackle repeat offenders, and we will continue to work closely with our partners to protect our business community.”
GPS tagging linked to reductions in offending among prolific shoplifters in Sussex

items.title: Consumer confidence hits two-year high but ‘could soon falter’
items.summary: Consumer confidence has surged to a two-year high in a surprise rise which will hand a much-needed boost to Andy Burnham ahead of the Budget – but experts have warned that momentum could soon run out. GfK’s closely-watched consumer confidence barometer rose to -13 in September, a rise of about one point since last month [...]
items.body:
Consumer confidence hits two-year high but ‘could soon falter’
Consumer confidence has surged to a two-year high in a surprise rise which will hand a much-needed boost to Andy Burnham ahead of the Budget – but experts have warned that momentum could soon run out.
GfK’s closely-watched consumer confidence barometer rose to -13 in September, a rise of about one point since last month and the highest level since August 2024.
The reading comes as a shock amid rising inflation and warnings from the Prime Minister that next month’s Budget will be “challenging” for the country.
Though consumer confidence remains in negative territory this is the first time since summer 2024 that GfK has delivered growth in the index three months in a row.
The biggest driver of September’s uplift in consumer confidence was Brits’ perceptions of the state of the economy over the past year, which eased by four points to -36.
Households’ attitudes towards their personal financial situation over the past year are also improving, easing by three points to -3. Brits’ perceptions of their financial situation for the coming year improved by one point to a reading of five points.
GfK’s September reading is the strongest signal yet that business saw a so-called “Burnham bounce” over the summer, helped by record temperatures and the FIFA World Cup.
Confidence ‘still firmly negative’
But Neil Bellamy, GfK’s consumer insights director, cautioned that this rebound could be running out of steam, as rising inflation threatens to ruin the mood.
He said: The return of higher inflation removes one of the strongest positives seen in previous months.
“So, while the headline score continues to improve, confidence is still firmly in negative territory. With inflation, energy and fuel prices rising, could we soon see consumer sentiment falter?”
Inflation rose from 2.9 to 3.1 per cent in August, as sharp rises in the price of petrol and diesel – along with higher air fares – outweighed steady food inflation.
Energy prices are showing no signs of meaningfully falling, prompting a Bank of England policymaker to warn on Thursday that interest rates may have to rise if energy costs stay high.
Clare Lombardelli, deputy governor of the central bank, told a conference in Warsaw that higher energy prices make it “increasingly likely” that monetary policy will need to be tightened.
The Bank of England left interest rates unchanged last week while the US’ Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank both opted to hike rates.

items.body:
JD.com gets physical as Kingfisher cashes in on AI: this week's biggest retail technology stories
It's Friday, the weekend is almost upon us, so let’s kick back and reflect on another eventful week for the retail tech space. Here's your briefing on the most important stories from the past few days, including Co-op, Instacart, StrongPoint, Dollar General, Morrisons, InPost UK, Asda, Thri5, and the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
1. Focus on 'seamless shopping upon seeing' experience as JD.com preps new 101Home store in Shanghai, China
JD.com reports that its first 101HOME store will open on 28th September in Jing’an District Shanghai. Building on the launch of an online flagship store in 2025, this is pitched as a premium lifestyle retail destination that brings together global design, home furnishing solution, smart technology, fashion, renovation services, dining, art and cultural experiences under one roof.
The retailer says that with its global sourcing capabilities, self-operated retail model and omnichannel infrastructure, 101HOME will offer a seamless “shopping upon seeing” experience, allowing consumers to explore new possibilities for their homes and discover the art of everyday living. Spanning approximately 12,000 square metres across four floors, 101HOME is designed to meet the evolving needs of consumers from age 0 to 101, across different life stages, household structures and lifestyles.
It brings together more than 1,000 full category home and lifestyle brands, including over 30 international brands making their China debut and more than 150 domestic and international brands making their JD.com debut. At the heart of 101HOME are 33 “Dream Homes”, designed for different living situation, family structures, lifestyles and interests.
The Shanghai store features spaces created by British designer Kelly Hoppen, and Japanese designers Shuhei Aoyama and Takashi Honma. Chinese designer Wang Heng (Ryan) draws on Song dynasty inspired aesthetics to create a three-generation family home. Consumers can step into fully designed home settings and see how furniture, lighting and furnishings come together, offering inspiration for their own homes.
2. Norwegian fashion retailer VILLOID inks deal with StrongPoint for world's largest Pio installation
StrongPoint has signed a contract with VILLOID, a Norwegian online fashion platform for women. This will see it design and install its new Pio facility, created by AutoStore, a warehouse automation solution.
The contract value is approximately NOK 17 million, and the installation is expected to be completed by Q2 2027.
VILLOID is moving its fulfilment centre to a new location, and the new Pio system will be doubled in size as the retailer requires additional capacity to support future growth. When completed the system is expected to be the largest Pio installation in the world.
"Retailers like VILLOID are looking for partners that understand their fulfilment operations, not just automation. That aligns with StrongPoint's focus on customer intimacy, working closely with customers to understand their operations, improve operational outcomes, and act as a partner rather than simply a supplier. We look forward to supporting VILLOID on its expanding automation journey," says Jacob Tverabaak, StrongPoint CEO.
"We have had a very positive experience with AutoStore Pio over several years. World class logistics with same-day delivery has been a key driver of our strong and profitable growth, delivering on customers' expectations of exceptional fulfilment service. StrongPoint will be a valuable partner as we continue our expansion, and with the new, larger Pio system we look forward to the additional capacity as we scale toward our next milestones. The facility will be the largest AutoStore Pio facility in the world," says Jeanette Dyhre Kvisvik, CEO and Founder at VILLOID.
3. Former McDonald's and Compass Group executive Jon Braithwaite connects with Co-op as new Group CDIO
Jon Braithwaite has joined Co-op as Interim Group Chief Digital and Information Officer. His CV includes stints at McDonald’s, Compass Group, and Gala Coral Group. Braithwaite is also an advisory board member at micro-donations specialist Pennies.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “Co-op is a business that combines commercial scale with genuine social purpose, and few organisations are as trusted. Technology sits right at the heart of how we serve member-owners, customers and colleagues. I'm looking forward to working with the brilliant team here and building on the momentum already underway. Exciting times ahead.”
4. AI startup Thri5 builds on Wild Fork Foods pilot as it lands $5.4 million in seed funding
Thri5 has announced $5.4 million in seed funding following a pilot and roll-out with Wild Fork Foods. The round was co-led by Whitecap Venture Partners and Mistral Venture Partners, with participation from MaRS Investment Accelerator Fund (IAF), N49P and a group of retail and technology veterans.
Wild Fork has deployed Thri5’s AI technology across its store network in the United States and Canada.
“What I look for in any new tool is whether it connects what’s happening on the floor with what we plan centrally, and whether the team can actually trust the data. Thri5 does both. Adoption was fast because it told operators what mattered each day, not just what to look at,” says Radek Mazurkiewicz, COO at Wild Fork Foods.
Thri5 is built as an AI native execution layer that develops context across the enterprise, understanding what is happening across the business, how work gets done and where value is being lost. It continuously interprets signals across a retailer’s data and systems, identifies and prioritises the highest value opportunities, and connects head office priorities with field and store execution, orchestrating action across teams, systems and AI agents.
As work is completed, Thri5 learns from outcomes, building deeper operational context and improving how the organisation executes over time. Because it sits above retailers’ existing technology stack, it can coordinate execution across functions without requiring them to replace or migrate their core systems.
5. Home improvement retailer Kingfisher taps AI tech driven personalisation as it ups profit target
Kingfisher Group, which owns B&Q and Screwfix in the UK and Castorama and Brico Depot in France and other markets, is using AI enabled productivity tools, including Fabric, to accelerate content creation, enhance SEO and improve conversion.
The FTSE 100 home improvement retailer lifted the lid on its AI and other tech initiatives as it raised its profit target despite seeing a heatwave driven drop off in sales at B&Q. It now expects to make a pre-tax profit of between £595 million and £635 million, having previously guided between £565 million and £625 million. Last year, it posted a £560 million profit.
Other highlights from its full year profit guidance and HY26/27 results include: group e-commerce sales reached 22% penetration. Group app sales now account for 29% of e-commerce sales, with app customers spending approximately 14% more than non-app users.
AI driven personalisation increased +16% generating approximately £100 million of sales, showing, Kingfisher claims, the growing value of its data and digital capabilities. Click & Collect sales were up +9% and home delivery sales +15%, supported by store-based fulfilment network and marketplace growth.
Screwfix Sprint (20 min delivery) was up +50% reflecting the growing demand for rapid fulfilment, particularly in Kingfisher’s City stores. Marketplace GMV rose +42% to £372 million, representing 18% of e-commerce sales. There has been investment in platform enhancements including Buybox, which helps customers find the best offer from multiple vendors by balancing price, merchant performance and delivery speed.
B&Q, meanwhile, continued to stump up cash for search and navigation capabilities, supporting improvements in online traffic and conversion. Natural language search is planned for implementation at B&Q in H2. The next phase of digital commerce will also include agent enabled shopping experiences.
6. InPost hails significant UK retail partnership as it inks Asda parcel lockers deal across 700 stores
Asda and InPost have announced a new partnership that will see up to 700 of the latter’s parcel lockers installed across the former’s UK store estate. This will give Asda customers a new way to send, collect and return parcels while they shop, and is pitched as one of InPost’s most significant UK retail partnerships to date.
The lockers will be installed across a mix of Asda superstores, supermarkets and Express locations.
Joseph Sutton, Director - Express, Fuel & Wholesale, says: "Our unmatched mix of services is a key part of what sets Asda apart, and we know customers increasingly value the convenience of being able to tick off multiple tasks in a single trip. We're delighted to be partnering with InPost to bring parcel lockers to up to 700 locations nationwide.
This roll-out gives customers a fast and flexible way to collect and return parcels, seamlessly fitting around their weekly shop and making everyday life a little easier."
7. UK grocery giant Morrisons names former Kingfisher executive Mohsen Ghasempour as Chief AI Officer
Morrisons has appointed Dr Mohsen Ghasempour as Chief AI Officer, a newly created role that will see him establish a central data science and AI function for the UK grocery retailer. He joins from Kingfisher, where he had served as Chief AI Officer since March 2024 following more than two years as Group AI Director.
He will take overall responsibility for data and AI strategy, with a remit spanning customer growth, colleague empowerment, operational efficiency, manufacturing excellence and commercial excellence. He will report directly to Morrisons CEO Rami Baitiéh when he takes up the role on 1st October.
“Creation of this new role reflects our commitment to ensuring Morrisons is embracing the opportunities in data and AI at pace, with focus and in the right way,” says Baitiéh.
“Mohsen is a recognised expert in the field with hands on experience of unlocking the potential of technology to deliver innovative new solutions that serve customers, empower colleagues and deliver measurable business impact.”
Ghasempour saus: “I’m excited about joining Morrisons and building the team that will help the business make effective and responsible use of AI in the years ahead, to deliver real benefits for customers and colleagues.”
8. Batteries Plus Director Karthik Jambulingam joins RTIH Innovation Awards judging panel for 2026
We're hugely pleased to announce the addition of Karthik Jambulingam, Senior Director of Enterprise Architecture, Batteries Plus, to the judging panel for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards. At Batteries Plus, he leads technology strategy and transformation across a 730+ store retail network in the United States.
With over 23 years in IT and a decade in technology leadership, he drives enterprise AI adoption, architecting multi-agent systems and agentic workflows for AI assisted selling, intelligent product discovery, and AI enabled decision-making in store operations, alongside a Gen AI assistant for store associates.
Karthik has also led the shift to cloud native, distributed architecture on Azure and Google Cloud, and modernised PoS and digital commerce platforms. He is a Senior Member of IEEE and holds an MBA and a B.E. in Computer Science.
Welcome onboard, Karthik!
Further information on our judging panel can be found here. In addition to Karthik, it includes representatives from Ingka Group/Ikea, JD Sports Fashion, Holland & Barrett, Walmart, CVS Health, Amazon, Boots, C&C Group, Warner Bros. Discovery, East of England Co-op, PoundFun, Austen & Blake, and Gordon Ramsay Restaurants.
9. Boots pilot launching on TikTok Shop in partnership with THG Commerce on 28th September
Boots UK is kicking off a TikTok Shop pilot, in partnership with THG Commerce, involving a curated selection of No7 skincare and beauty products. Further brands and products are set to launch over the coming months.
Paula Bobbett, Chief Digital and Data Officer at Boots, says: “Millions of people are already discovering beauty and skincare products through TikTok and the creators and communities that they trust. This launch gives us an exciting new way to be part of this dynamic experience and help more customers to discover new products and shop those they love in way that feels seamless and relevant to their lives.”
Daniel Callaghan, Business Development Manager at THG Ingenuity, says: “Boots' debut on TikTok Shop is a testament to the growth and development that the platform has seen over the last few years. This forms part of Boots’ wider ambition to create more connected customer experiences and bring beauty content, product discovery and purchase closer together. Through the platform, it aims to reach new audiences, while giving existing customers greater choice and flexibility in how and where they shop. Huge move, and well done to everyone involved.”
10. Dollar General and Instacart on demand delivery partnership kicks off with pilot across six US states
Instacart and Dollar General have announced a new partnership to offer same-day delivery of the latter’s everyday essentials through the former’s app and website. The partnership will launch with a pilot at approximately 7,000 Dollar General and pOpshelf stores in six states in the coming weeks with plans to expand to approximately 20,000 stores across 48 states this autumn.
“Dollar General’s vast footprint and longstanding commitment to affordability make them an important addition to the Instacart Marketplace,” says Ryan Hamburger, Chief Commercial Officer at Instacart. “As we expand this partnership to approximately 20,000 Dollar General and pOpshelf stores, we’ll help provide customers in communities across the country with even greater access to affordable food and everyday essentials, with the convenience of same-day delivery.”
“Our mission is Serving Others, and we continually look for new ways to provide customers with the value and convenience they count on," says Tony Rogers, Senior Vice President and Chief Marketing Officer at Dollar General. "Our partnership with Instacart provides another convenient way for customers to access affordable food, household essentials and other products they need while saving them valuable time."

items.body:
Just one week left to submit your entries for the industry leading 2026 RTIH Technology Innovation Awards
The entry deadline for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards is fast approaching. The big day is Friday, 2nd October. That’s just one week away, so don’t delay, start working on your submissions today!
The awards, sponsored by 3D Cloud, Business France, and Retail Technology Show 2027, celebrate global tech innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world. Our latest winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC (Prince Consort Rooms) in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Further information on our judging panel can be found here. The panel includes representatives from JD Sports Fashion, Holland & Barrett, Batteries Plus, Walmart, Amazon, CVS Health, Boots, C&C Group, Warner Bros. Discovery, East of England Co-op, PoundFun, Austen & Blake, and Gordon Ramsay Restaurants.
Click here for FAQs and categories.
Sign up for an account and submit your entry or entries here.
Key dates for 2026
Friday, 20th February: Awards open for entries
Friday, 2nd October: Awards entry deadline
Tuesday, 6th October: 2026 finalists revealed
Wednesday, 7th October - 20th October: Judging days
Wednesday, 4th November: Winners announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC (Prince Consort Rooms) in Central London.
Please email our awards team if you have any questions or need further information: awards@retailtechinnovationhub.com
FAQs
Is there a fee to enter the awards?: It is free to enter and you can do so across multiple categories.
Do I need to complete all the sections in the entry form? No, but the more information you provide, the better chance you have of producing a successful submission.
Is there a certain timeframe for nominated projects, initiatives etc? Yes, nominated projects, initiatives etc should have been completed (or substantially completed) during the last 12 months.
Who has visibility of our completed entry form and what information will be public should we win or be shortlisted? Only our Editor, Scott Thompson, and judging panel will view submissions. The information provided in the summary section of the entry form will be made public.
Do you only accept entries from UK-based companies? No, we accept entries from all parts of the world.
What is the shortlists process? Shortlists will be announced in October, then shortlisted entries will be sent to our independent judging panel who will decide upon the winners and highly commended submissions.
Shortlisted companies will be invited to attend an event at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November (consisting of a drinks reception, three course meal and awards ceremony).
Do winners and highly commended companies receive post-event coverage? Yes, post-event coverage includes articles on our website and also an in-depth awards review in our printed magazine. There is also the opportunity for a company profile type piece to be published on our site.

items.body:
Paul Smith wraps deployment of Sitoo retail technology across all its stores and global markets
Paul Smith has completed its roll-out of Sitoo’s cloud native unified commerce and PoS platform for fashion and lifestyle retailers across 31 stores in eight countries. In a LinkedIn post, Sitoo said: “A major milestone with an amazing customer!”
It added: “After months of close collaboration, it’s fantastic to see Sitoo now live across all Paul Smith stores and markets - and even more exciting to think about what comes next. A huge thank you to the brilliant teams at Paul Smith and Sitoo who made this milestone possible. We’re incredibly proud of what we’ve achieved together and excited to continue working closely as our partnership grows. Here’s to the next chapter!”
Start spreading the news
Sweden founded Sitoo recently opened its first US office in New York.
A company spokesperson said: “Opening an office in the heart of the Big Apple is the next step to bringing the success we’ve seen in Europe to retailers across North America. It's not where our US story starts, though.”
“That began in 2018 when Nudie Jeans implemented Sitoo in their US stores and continued in 2023 when Rally House chose Sitoo to power its fast growing store network. Since then we’ve seen more store openings throughout the country alongside building thriving partnerships with amazing companies like Zebra, Adyen and Bloomreach. The office is what comes next.”
CEO and Co-founder Jens Levin commented: "The US is a competitive market, but we’re fully confident in our ability to succeed. We bridge a critical gap by combining enterprise robustness with modern agility. Our Scandinavian approach to efficient, fast, and reliable global execution is a great advantage and something we know will be a real point of difference.”
So hot right now
Sitoo is included in RTIH’s first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. Launching in August, this sees us bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
Our Founder and Editor, Scott Thompson, drew up a list of 150 companies that had consistently been on his radar over the past 12 months whilst bringing our community the latest retail tech news and views that matter. These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position.
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…
Editor and Founder of Retail Technology Innovation Hub

items.body:
Aldi claims on demand delivery first in UK discount supermarket space as retailer teams with Deliveroo
From October, Aldi UK will be trialling a new partnership with Deliveroo across eight UK stores, giving customers access to its full grocery range through the on demand delivery firm’s app. Modelled on Aldi’s partnerships with DoorDash, Deliveroo’s parent company, in the United States and Australia, the latter’s riders will pick, pack and deliver orders directly from stores.
The trial is pitched as the only rapid delivery service available from a discount supermarket in the UK.
Customers will be able to order around 2,000 Aldi products, including fresh fruit and vegetables, meat, dairy, bread, household essentials and Specialbuys. They can order on-demand or choose a delivery window that suits them. A nationwide launch is currently planned for early 2027.
Giles Hurley, Chief Executive Officer at Aldi UK, says: “We’ve always been committed to bringing low prices to as many people as possible, and this partnership with Deliveroo allows us to do exactly that without changing how our stores operate. The DoorDash model has been incredibly popular with Aldi customers in Australia and the United States, and we know from our previous trial there is clear demand for more affordable groceries on a rapid delivery platform in the UK. By working with Deliveroo, we can give more people access to Aldi quality and value, however they choose to shop with us.”
Rob Harris, VP Merchant and Chief Revenue Officer at Deliveroo, says: “We are excited to welcome Aldi to the Deliveroo platform through a brand new service, Shop & Deliver. Customers in several locations across the country will soon be able to enjoy Aldi’s great value and selection delivered to their doorstep on demand.”
“For riders, Shop & Deliver is entirely optional, offering an additional way to earn outside of busy mealtimes, which often suits those who choose to ride alongside childcare or another form of work.”

And this week we’re focusing on LolaLiza which has opened a new store featuring a custom AI fashion avatar created by Screenix. Displayed on a Samsung spatial screen and brought into the store in conjunction with DOBIT, the avatar aims to showcase LolaLiza’s collections in a fresh and dynamic way.
A spokesperson for Screenix says: “It turns traditional digital signage into dynamic inspirational content that feels completely at home in the physical retail environment. A great example of how technology, content and strong partnerships can create more engaging in-store experiences.”
They add: “A big thank you to LolaLiza for the trust, and to Samsung Display Solutions and DOBIT for the great collaboration. Congratulations to the entire LolaLiza team on the opening. We’re proud to be part of it.”
And honourable mentions this week to...
Tesco
Tesco is introducing new virtual try-on technology for the first time, as part of a trial at its Sandhurst Extra store. Powered by AIUTA tech, the experience lets customers virtually try on around 1,500 items of F&F clothing across womenswear and menswear by taking a photo or uploading a photo of themselves onto a digital try-on screen in the clothing department, or selecting a digital model to view clothes in different sizes.
The trial is designed to understand how Tesco can help customers browsing in-store to discover new styles and feel more confident before they buy.
The virtual try-on screen forms part of a wider F&F refresh at Sandhurst Extra, which includes new changing rooms and a dedicated service hub for easier checking out and returns. Customers will also see a larger F&F range in-store and a refreshed look and feel with new signage, updated lighting and a focus on showcasing the F&F range across womenswear, menswear and childrenswear.
JD.com
JD.com reports that its first 101HOME store will open on 28th September in Jing’an District Shanghai.
Building on the launch of an online flagship store in 2025, this is pitched as a premium lifestyle retail destination that brings together global design, home furnishing solution, smart technology, fashion, renovation services, dining, art and cultural experiences under one roof.
The retailer says that with its global sourcing capabilities, self-operated retail model and omnichannel infrastructure, 101HOME will offer a seamless “shopping upon seeing” experience, allowing consumers to explore new possibilities for their homes and discover the art of everyday living. Spanning approximately 12,000 square metres across four floors, 101HOME is designed to meet the evolving needs of consumers from age 0 to 101, across different life stages, household structures and lifestyles.
It brings together more than 1,000 full category home and lifestyle brands, including over 30 international brands making their China debut and more than 150 domestic and international brands making their JD.com debut. At the heart of 101HOME are 33 “Dream Homes”, designed for different living situation, family structures, lifestyles and interests.
The Shanghai store features spaces created by British designer Kelly Hoppen, and Japanese designers Shuhei Aoyama and Takashi Honma. Chinese designer Wang Heng (Ryan) draws on Song dynasty inspired aesthetics to create a three-generation family home. Consumers can step into fully designed home settings and see how furniture, lighting and furnishings come together, offering inspiration for their own homes.
“101HOME is designed to go beyond traditional home retailing, bringing together home design, lifestyle trends and social experiences under one roof,” says Billy Bao, Head of 101HOME at JD.com. “We want to create a unique experience where consumers can discover new products, explore different ways of living and find inspiration for their own homes. With JD.com’s global sourcing and supply chain capabilities, we can help turn that inspiration into reality, making it easier for consumers to create a home that reflects their individual lifestyles.”
Powered by JD.com’s JoyAI and JoyInside technologies, smart home solutions demonstrate applications across entry systems, kitchens, bathrooms, sleep and health management. The store also features dozens of robotic products. There is also a here cafe, a popular coffee brand from Kyoto; ICE BOUQUET, known for its floral inspired gelato; JUANZONG Books; DEVINE’R NYC, a New York coffee and lifestyle brand; and Foyer de Lumiere, a Japanese-French bistro, several of which are making their mainland China or Shanghai debuts.
101HOME also offers more than 300 Burgundy wines, with over 100 available by the glass. Seven public artworks are also integrated across different floors and public spaces. The experience is accessible digitally through a WeChat mini programme and the JD.com app.
VILLOID
StrongPoint has signed a contract with VILLOID, a Norwegian online fashion platform for women. This will see it design and install its new Pio facility, created by AutoStore, a warehouse automation solution.
The contract value is approximately NOK 17 million, and the installation is expected to be completed by Q2 2027.
VILLOID is moving its fulfilment centre to a new location, and the new Pio system will be doubled in size as the retailer requires additional capacity to support future growth. When completed the system is expected to be the largest Pio installation in the world.
"Retailers like VILLOID are looking for partners that understand their fulfilment operations, not just automation. That aligns with StrongPoint's focus on customer intimacy, working closely with customers to understand their operations, improve operational outcomes, and act as a partner rather than simply a supplier. We look forward to supporting VILLOID on its expanding automation journey," says Jacob Tverabaak, StrongPoint CEO.
"We have had a very positive experience with AutoStore Pio over several years. World class logistics with same-day delivery has been a key driver of our strong and profitable growth, delivering on customers' expectations of exceptional fulfilment service. StrongPoint will be a valuable partner as we continue our expansion, and with the new, larger Pio system we look forward to the additional capacity as we scale toward our next milestones. The facility will be the largest AutoStore Pio facility in the world," says Jeanette Dyhre Kvisvik, CEO and Founder at VILLOID.

items.body:
Loyalty programme fails, AI successes, and refundjacking rises: the retail technology week in numbers
Do you like numbers? Do you like retail tech news? Then this is the article for you. Including JD.com, KIngfisher Group, RTIH magazine, Thri5, StrongPoint, Ryft, HyperFinity, Fleek, Adobe, Royal Mail, StrongPoint, and Simbe.

11...The eleventh issue of RTIH magazine is now available, packed with must read interviews, thought leadership pieces, industry deep dives, and the latest technology innovations transforming the global retail sector.
With thanks to our supporters: 3D Cloud, Aptos, Hanshow, Everseen, Foundit!, Orquest, Datitude, Sitoo, Star Micronics, Retec, Retail Express, Broadsign, Fynd, and Sitoo.
£595 million and £635 million...Kingfisher Group, which owns B&Q and Screwfix in the UK and Castorama and Brico Depot in France and other markets, is using AI enabled productivity tools, including Fabric, to accelerate content creation, enhance SEO and improve conversion.
The FTSE 100 home improvement retailer lifted the lid on its AI and other tech initiatives as it raised its profit target despite seeing a heatwave driven drop off in sales at B&Q. It now expects to make a pre-tax profit of between £595 million and £635 million, having previously guided between £565 million and £625 million. Last year, it posted a £560 million profit.
Other highlights from its full year profit guidance and HY26/27 results include: group e-commerce sales reached 22% penetration. Group app sales now account for 29% of e-commerce sales, with app customers spending approximately 14% more than non-app users.
AI driven personalisation increased +16% generating approximately £100 million of sales, showing, Kingfisher claims, the growing value of its data and digital capabilities. Click & Collect sales were up +9% and home delivery sales +15%, supported by store-based fulfilment network and marketplace growth.
Screwfix Sprint (20 min delivery) was up +50% reflecting the growing demand for rapid fulfilment, particularly in Kingfisher’s City stores. Marketplace GMV rose +42% to £372 million, representing 18% of e-commerce sales. There has been investment in platform enhancements including Buybox, which helps customers find the best offer from multiple vendors by balancing price, merchant performance and delivery speed.
B&Q, meanwhile, continued to stump up cash for search and navigation capabilities, supporting improvements in online traffic and conversion. Natural language search is planned for implementation at B&Q in H2. The next phase of digital commerce will also include agent enabled shopping experiences.
$5.4 million...Thri5 has announced $5.4 million in seed funding following a pilot and roll-out with Wild Fork Foods. The round was co-led by Whitecap Venture Partners and Mistral Venture Partners, with participation from MaRS Investment Accelerator Fund (IAF), N49P and a group of retail and technology veterans.
Wild Fork has deployed Thri5’s AI technology across its store network in the United States and Canada.
“What I look for in any new tool is whether it connects what’s happening on the floor with what we plan centrally, and whether the team can actually trust the data. Thri5 does both. Adoption was fast because it told operators what mattered each day, not just what to look at,” says Radek Mazurkiewicz, COO at Wild Fork Foods.
Thri5 is built as an AI native execution layer that develops context across the enterprise, understanding what is happening across the business, how work gets done and where value is being lost. It continuously interprets signals across a retailer’s data and systems, identifies and prioritises the highest value opportunities, and connects head office priorities with field and store execution, orchestrating action across teams, systems and AI agents.
As work is completed, Thri5 learns from outcomes, building deeper operational context and improving how the organisation executes over time. Because it sits above retailers’ existing technology stack, it can coordinate execution across functions without requiring them to replace or migrate their core systems.
NOK 17 million...StrongPoint has signed a contract with VILLOID, a Norwegian online fashion platform for women. This will see it design and install its new Pio facility, created by AutoStore, a warehouse automation solution.
The contract value is approximately NOK 17 million, and the installation is expected to be completed by Q2 2027.
VILLOID is moving its fulfilment centre to a new location, and the new Pio system will be doubled in size as the retailer requires additional capacity to support future growth. When completed the system is expected to be the largest Pio installation in the world.
"Retailers like VILLOID are looking for partners that understand their fulfilment operations, not just automation. That aligns with StrongPoint's focus on customer intimacy, working closely with customers to understand their operations, improve operational outcomes, and act as a partner rather than simply a supplier. We look forward to supporting VILLOID on its expanding automation journey," says Jacob Tverabaak, StrongPoint CEO.
"We have had a very positive experience with AutoStore Pio over several years. World class logistics with same-day delivery has been a key driver of our strong and profitable growth, delivering on customers' expectations of exceptional fulfilment service. StrongPoint will be a valuable partner as we continue our expansion, and with the new, larger Pio system we look forward to the additional capacity as we scale toward our next milestones. The facility will be the largest AutoStore Pio facility in the world," says Jeanette Dyhre Kvisvik, CEO and Founder at VILLOID.
51 of the UK’s leading retailers are collectively missing out on £806.9 million in gross margin each year through loyalty programmes that fail to convert member engagement into genuine commercial return, according to HyperFinity research.
This finds that the average retailer is sitting on £15.8 million of untapped gross margin opportunity tied up in underperforming loyalty programmes. Crucially, the analysis shows this is not a crisis of customer loyalty itself, but a crisis of execution.
Recent consumer research from HyperFinity found that 91% of shoppers use their loyalty programmes on every visit or most visits, and 79% want more personalised offers. However, the intelligence to turn that participation into genuine commercial value remains largely untapped.
HyperFinity says it has identified three failure modes that appear most consistently across underperforming programmes: Redemption friction: where personalised rewards cannot actually be used by the customer; Value erosion: programmes dilute their value over time and customers no longer feel recognised or personally rewarded; App performance: where technical issues can undermine the loyalty experience at key moments of engagement. Between them, these three issues account for the vast majority of loyalty underperformance across the 51 retailers analysed.
Grocery and sports retail represent the largest sectors of untapped loyalty value in the analysis. In grocery, where loyalty programmes are near-universal and consumer expectations are high, the gap between programme promise and programme delivery is particularly pronounced. In sports retail, high basket values and strong brand affinity mean the commercial cost of underperformance is further amplified.
28%...Selling secondhand clothes is no longer just a way to make a bit of extra cash. New research from AI powered resale marketplace Fleek finds that 28% of resellers now do it full-time, with a further third actively working to turn their side hustle into a career.
Its report, compiled from millions of its platform’s real-time search and sales signals alongside responses from 339 resellers in 22 countries, found that the longer people remain in this space, the more likely they are to turn it into a full-time job, with just 14% of those selling for less than six months working full-time, compared with 53% of those who have been doing it for more than five years. It also found that almost two-thirds of full-timers say resale now accounts for the majority of their income.
Across generations, Millennial resellers are 81% more likely than average to cite flexibility or childcare as a reason for reselling, while Gen X sellers are more likely to view resale as a way to replace a job.
Resellers find it beneficial to spread sales across multiple platforms. Vinted is the most popular, with 65% claiming it earns them more money than any other platform.
27%...Refundjacking - where shoppers gain from a company’s refund policies - is becoming one of e-commerce’s biggest challenges. New research from fraud prevention platform Ravelin revealed 27% of people openly admit to abusing refund policies.
The research is based on a survey of 6,282 consumers, drawn from the UK (2,115), Germany (2,095), and France (2,072) who have shopped online in the last six months. 98% of attempts to take advantage of these systems are successful. 37% of UK consumers have engaged in, or plan to engage in, refund abuse, according to the major European markets surveyed, making the UK the highest rate of refundjacking - higher than France (33%) and Germany (25%).
Behaviours include gaming refund and return polices, falsely claiming goods never arrived, returning items after using them or sending back empty boxes or dummy returns while keeping the original product. Research shows that occasional abusers are earning an average of €/£390 per claim, where shoppers who abuse the policies more than four times a year can an average of €/£491 per claim.
The British Retail Consortium’s Policy Advisor for Finance, Chris Owen, comments “The growth of refund abuse is putting unnecessary financial drain on retailers at a time when margins are already under intense pressure. The result is lost revenue and higher costs, meaning everyone ends up paying more. It’s a serious problem which requires serious attention. The BRC is working with our members and others to tackle this growing problem.
3,000…Royal Mail has announced the acquisition of Quadient’s UK-based parcel locker network. Around 3,000 lockers will now become part of Royal Mail’s out of home network. The transaction is expected to close by the end of the calendar year. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.
A Royal Mail spokesperson said: “Together with our existing lockers, parcel shops and parcel postboxes, this acquisition will further enhance our out of home network of 30,000 parcel points and strengthen our proposition for customers. This is an exciting step forward in making it even easier for customers to send, collect and return parcels in the way that suits them best, through lockers, shops and other convenient locations.”
The deal strengthens Royal Mail’s position and makes it a major player in a crowded UK parcel lockers market that also includes InPost, Amazon, and YEEP!
3,000...Simbe reports that it has surpassed 3,000 autonomous units under contract, which is pitched as the largest commercially committed fleet of shelf intelligence technology (as identified in the company's research).
In the decade since introducing Tally, an inventory robot, Simbe has been shifting from autonomous shelf digitisation to building a broader platform for the physical store.
Today, Simbe combines autonomous robots, computer vision, RFID, handheld and fixed sensing to continuously capture what is happening inside retail locations: from inventory availability and product location to prices, promotions, and merchandising conditions.
“Retailers are increasingly deploying physical intelligence across the enterprise,” says Deborah Weinswig, Founder and CEO at Coresight Research. “Simbe’s 3,000 unit milestone reflects that shift: trusted shelf-level data is becoming foundational to store operations, digital commerce, merchandising and supply chain decisions.”
Highlights include: More than 75 retail banners globally, including BJ’s Wholesale Club, Kroger, and SPAR; The first and only company to earn UL 3300 certification for a robot designed to operate in public; More than 90% of store managers working alongside Tally say the technology makes their jobs better.
149%...Adobe has released a new report, based on analysis of over ten billion transactions every month, revealing headline UK spending figures from January to August and how online shopping behaviours are shifting thanks to AI.
UK online spending has grown steadily in 2026 - up 3.9% YTD. Spending growth accelerated from early summer onwards, with June the highest spending month of the year so far (£10.6 billion, up 16.9% YoY), primarily caused by Amazon Prime Day occurring in June this year rather than July.
YoY growth in traffic to retail sites from AI sources peaked in August, up 149% YoY and up more than 1,400% compared with October 2024. Conversion rates from AI traffic sources (which, in the UK, overtook those from non-AI traffic for the first time) were 20% higher than non-AI channels in August.
700...Asda and InPost have announced a new partnership that will see up to 700 of the latter’s parcel lockers installed across the former’s UK store estate. This will give Asda customers a new way to send, collect and return parcels while they shop, and is pitched as one of InPost’s most significant UK retail partnerships to date.
The lockers will be installed across a mix of Asda superstores, supermarkets and Express locations.
Joseph Sutton, Director - Express, Fuel & Wholesale, says: "Our unmatched mix of services is a key part of what sets Asda apart, and we know customers increasingly value the convenience of being able to tick off multiple tasks in a single trip. We're delighted to be partnering with InPost to bring parcel lockers to up to 700 locations nationwide.
This roll-out gives customers a fast and flexible way to collect and return parcels, seamlessly fitting around their weekly shop and making everyday life a little easier."
£20 million...Manchester-based payments company Ryft has secured a £20 million Series B led by Gresham House Ventures. More than 6,500 businesses, including Epos Now, Chaiwalla, the Disasters Emergency Committee, Daytrip and Sprive, are now using its payment system. The investment, which takes the total raised to date to approximately £27 million, will support Ryft’s expansion across Europe and the US, while accelerating its product development and move upmarket.
As part of its European expansion, Ryft has applied for a full EU license from the Malta Financial Services Authority (MFSA). With this, Ryft will be able to passport its services across the European Economic Area. The round also featured participation from existing investors Pembroke VCT and Ingenii Capital.
Ryft’s CEO and Co-founder, Sadra Hosseini comments: “This round of investment means we can take what we’ve built in the UK into new European markets and compete on the global stage. Payments have been dominated by a small number of incumbents for a long time. We want to provide a powerful and efficient alternative to businesses, not just in Europe, but globally.”

items.body:
Smythson enlists ESW as it builds on UK and US presence and looks to reach more customers globally
ESW has announced a partnership with British luxury lifestyle brand, Smythson, to support its international e-commerce growth plans.
Founded in 1887 and known for its leather diaries, notebooks, travel bags and accessories, Smythson has built a customer base across the UK, United States and international markets. ESW will support its US and rest of world e-commerce operations, providing the cross-border commerce infrastructure needed to deliver a seamless customer experience across international markets and support future growth ambitions.
Seb Villien, Digital & Logistics Director at Smythson, says: “As we continue to expand Smythson’s global presence, working with a partner like ESW allows us to reach customers beyond our core markets, while always maintaining our focus on the quality and experience our brand is known for.”
Tonia Luykx, Chief Revenue Officer at ESW, says: “Smythson has spent almost 140 years building a distinctive British luxury brand with customers around the world. By taking on the complexity of cross-border commerce, we can help them reach even more of those customers and create a foundation for its next phase of international e-commerce growth.”
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
E-commerce will be a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards are now open for entries and celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world.
Our winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Check out our 2025 winners here.
Our 2025 hall of fame entrants were revealed during a sold out event which took place at The HAC on 16th October and consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, and awards ceremony presided over by award winning comedian, actress and writer Tiff Stevenson.
In his welcome speech, Scott Thompson, Founder and Editor, RTIH, said: “This is the awards’ fifth year as a physical event. We started off with just 30 people at the South Place Hotel not far from here, then moved to London Bridge Hotel, then The Barbican, and last year RIBA’s HQ in the West End.”
“But I’m conscious of the fact that, to quote the legend that is Taylor Swift, You’re only as hot as your last hit, baby. So, this year we’ve moved to our biggest venue yet, and also pulled in our largest number of entries to date and broken attendance records.”
He added: “This year’s submissions have without doubt been our best yet. To quote one of the judges: The examples of innovative developments across both traditional and digital retail spaces were truly remarkable.”
Congratulations to our winners, and a big thank you to our sponsors, judging panel, the legend that is Tiff Stevenson, and all those who attended our 2025 gathering.
Editor and Founder of Retail Technology Innovation Hub

items.title: Retail struggles see Dragon's Den star sell photo firm Jessops as DFS says sofa sales are suffering
items.summary: The TV star and businessman Peter Jones (pictured) rescued the firm out of administration in 2013 and re-opened a raft of closed stores.
items.body:
Retail struggles see Dragon's Den star sell photo firm Jessops as DFS says sofa sales are suffering
Dragons’ Den investor Peter Jones has sold camera retailer Jessops to AO World.
The TV star and businessman rescued the firm out of administration in 2013 and re-opened a raft of closed stores.
But Jessops collapsed into administration again in 2019 and once more in 2021 amid changes in the camera market. It now has just eight stores – down from more than 250 at its height.
Jones has sold it to the electricals supplier for an undisclosed sum. AO World founder and chief executive John Roberts said: ‘I am delighted to welcome Jessops into the AO family and look forward to growing the existing business as well as integrating the category into the wider AO business.’
The group said the move supports its strategy to grow into ‘adjacent categories, giving customers and members more reasons to shop’ and encouraging them to spend greater amounts.
But shares in AO World – which bought online retailer Music Magpie in December 2024 – fell 4.5 per cent as it gave a more cautious outlook on second-half trading.
Dragons’ Den investor Peter Jones recued camera retailer Jessops out of administration in 2013 and re-opened a raft of closed stores
DFS has warned it is ‘cautious’ about the economic outlook – as retailers slashed orders from suppliers by the most since records began more than 40 years ago.
The furniture seller, which boasts a partnership with Britain’s Got Talent judge Amanda Holden, said sales fell 2.6 per cent in the past 12 weeks.
The update came as the CBI said retailers have suffered their biggest drop in sales since April and cut orders from their suppliers at the fastest rate since records began in 1983.
‘Retailers reported a steep fall in annual sales volumes in September,’ said Martin Sartorius, lead economist at the CBI.
‘The persistent sales downturn appears to have prompted retailers to cut back on order volumes at a survey-record pace.’

items.body:
Hotel Chocolat, the luxury British chocolatier and cacao grower known for its imaginative chocolates and distinctive retail experiences, is accelerating its U.S. growth in three new markets and an expanded presence across retail and travel channels.
The brand will open stores at Fashion Place in Salt Lake City, Utah; 2ND & PCH in Long Beach, California; and King Street in Alexandria, Virginia, beginning in late fall 2026.
Hotel Chocolat will also broaden its retail distribution through partnerships with Wegmans, H-E-B, and Kroger and expand its reach within major U.S. airports through a partnership with Paradies Lagardère.
These moves coincide with an increasingly accessible ecommerce experience for Hotel Chocolat that allows the brand to reach even more online shoppers. Along with its sophisticated Hotel Chocolat USA direct-to-consumer website, Hotel Chocolat has grown its presence on TikTok Shop and Amazon via dedicated, branded storefronts that bring an enhanced product portfolio directly to millions of existing customers, making everyday discovery and gifting seamless.
“Hotel Chocolat is moving to our next phase of growth in the U.S.,” said Kelly Goering, general manager of Hotel Chocolat US. “By opening stores in three distinctive new markets across the country, expanding through leading retail and travel partners, and enhancing our ecommerce offerings, we are creating more ways for more customers to discover and enjoy all of our inventive chocolate options. We are growing thoughtfully – selecting the right markets, locations and partners while preserving the creativity, quality and sense of wonder that define the Hotel Chocolat experience.”
Each new store will bring Hotel Chocolat to a setting that reflects the character of its surrounding community, taking lessons from the brand’s thoughtful expansion and success across its six Chicago-area locations. The Salt Lake City store will be located within Fashion Place, one of Utah’s premier shopping destinations. In Long Beach, Hotel Chocolat will join the shops and restaurants of 2ND & PCH, a vibrant open-air destination along the Southern California coast. The Alexandria, Virginia, store will bring the brand to historic King Street, known for its distinctive mix of independent shops, restaurants and cultural attractions.
Guests at the new stores will discover an extensive selection of Hotel Chocolat’s signature chocolates, including offerings like:
- The over 100 recipes in the iconic Hotel Chocolat “Wall of Chocolate,” with flavors ranging from tipsy Salted Espresso Martini, dreamy Tiramisu, and fruity Raspberry & Pistachio Chocolate selectors. Chocolate lovers can mix and match any three for $20.
- The imaginative Christmas and Holiday collection, featuring Hotel Chocolat’s signature Grand Wreath Box, that’s packed in a striking, circular red box with an inner-lid menu of treats; whimsical stocking stuffers like The Sleigh Team, A Dozen Gingerbread Men, and Portly Penguins; and a variety of Advent Calendars like The Advent Calendar for Two, which features two identical mini truffles in a variety of flavors behind each door.
- Boxed chocolate gifting options that can be personalized for every occasion – from Happy Birthday, Thank You, Congratulations, to Just Because – in signature flavor profiles like the Milk Devotee 29 Pack, Patisserie Dreamer 27 Pack, Serious Dark Fix 29 Pack and many more.
- The Velvetiser Café, serving the brand’s hot and cold drinking chocolate options in over eighteen delicious flavors like Salted Caramel, Mint, and Coconut-White.
- The Wall of Velvetiser, where guests can mix and match drinking chocolate flavors, designing their own box to enjoy at home.
Beyond its company-operated stores, Hotel Chocolat is broadening its U.S. retail footprint through partnerships with Wegmans, H-E-B, and select banners with Kroger. The offerings in some of these locations will include designated branded displays featuring shelf ready packaging as well as header and side panel signage that serve to pique shopper interest and extend the world of Hotel Chocolat beyond the shelves themselves. These partnerships will make the brand available to more consumers in the places they already shop, deepening Hotel Chocolat’s reach into new markets and occasions.
Starting November 1, shoppers with Wegmans will be able to buy a selection of Hotel Chocolat’s delightful stocking stuffer chocolates and Advent calendars; shoppers with H-E-B can try the reindeer-shaped milk chocolates of Sleigh Team; and Kroger fans will be able to purchase the Hotel Chocolat Milk, Dark, and Caramel-Milk Advent Calendars, along with all of the stocking stuffers.
The brand is also growing its presence in U.S. airports through Paradies Lagardère, a leading travel retailer and restaurateur operating more than 700 retail, dining and bar locations across more than 90 airports. The partnership will expand Hotel Chocolat’s reach among travelers at over seventy retail locations across just under fifty major hubs, including John F. Kennedy International Airport, Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, Los Angeles International Airport, and Dallas Fort Worth International Airport, where travelers will be able to purchase the iconic Enchanted Forest stocking stuffer when traveling domestically.
“Together with our retail and travel partnerships, our new market expansion marks an important step forward for Hotel Chocolat in the U.S.,” added Goering. “They allow us to meet customers in more of the places they live, shop and travel, and introduces them to what makes Hotel Chocolat distinctive: our deep connection to cacao, imaginative approach to chocolate and commitment to making every interaction with us feel special. This is about building a thoughtful, lasting presence in the U.S., one market and one customer relationship at a time.”
Additional details, including individual store opening dates and hours, will be announced in the coming months. Fans who want to explore Hotel Chocolat’s unique collections in advance can visit us.hotelchocolat.com or Hotel Chocolat on Amazon.

items.title: The end of de minimis demands a delivery reset
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Rory O’Connor CEO at delivery management platform Scurri warns e-commerce retailers not to simply think about a customs workaround but look again at all their processes and provides seven key actions The end of de minimis customs exemptions means that the international e-commerce model based around large assortments, competitive prices and high volumes of low-value […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Rory O’Connor CEO at delivery management platform Scurri warns e-commerce retailers not to simply think about a customs workaround but look again at all their processes and provides seven key actions
The end of de minimis customs exemptions means that the international e-commerce model based around large assortments, competitive prices and high volumes of low-value parcels sent directly to consumers is over, at least for some companies as we have been reading in the media.
After the EU abolished its exemption for consignments worth up to €150, introducing an interim €3 duty on low-value imported items from July 2026, the immediate result was higher costs and greater complexity. But retailers should resist treating this as simply another charge to absorb or pass on. It challenges the commercial assumptions behind product pricing, fulfilment location, carrier selection, delivery promises and returns. The answer should not be a temporary customs workaround, but a redesign of the cross-border delivery model.
- Establish the true landed cost of every order
Retailers first need to understand the complete landed cost of an order at product, basket and destination level. This should include transport, duties, taxes, clearance charges, carrier surcharges, failed deliveries and potential returns.
An average figure applied across the business will not be sufficient. A €3 duty may have little effect on a high-value product but destroy the margin on a low-priced item. In the EU, the charge can also apply to different item categories within a parcel, making its composition as important as its overall value.
Scurri research among 150 large UK retailers indicates that many lack the necessary visibility. Only 35% have clear visibility and a defined cost for the principal delivery errors affecting their operations. 38% track some but not all costs, while another 25% cannot measure them precisely or have little visibility.
- Reconsider where inventory sits
Retailers sending individual parcels from distant source markets should compare that model with importing inventory in bulk and fulfilling orders regionally. Consolidated imports followed by domestic distribution may prove more economical than clearing thousands of consumer parcels separately.
Regional inventory brings its own risks, including forecasting errors, additional working capital and unsold stock. A hybrid approach may therefore work better; fast-moving lines can sit closer to customers, while specialist or less predictable products continue to be fulfilled internationally.
The decision should reflect order density, product value, demand predictability, delivery expectations and returns volumes rather than a single global fulfilment rule.
- Make carrier selection dynamic
The end of de minimis changes the relative economics of carriers and delivery services. A service that was competitive under simplified duty free arrangements may no longer provide the best combination of cost, customs clearance and delivery performance.
Retailers should avoid hardwiring international orders to one carrier. Selection should respond dynamically to destination, product category, order value, customs requirements and promised delivery date.
A delivery management platform can apply these rules to each order, while enabling retailers to introduce alternative services without rebuilding their checkout and warehouse systems. It also provides the data needed to compare expected costs with carrier invoices, delivery outcomes and surcharges.
This is important as retailers pursue greater overseas growth. 17% of those surveyed by Scurri plan international ecommerce expansion during the next year, despite a similar proportion expecting tariffs to increase consumer prices.
- Remove customs surprises from the customer experience
Retailers must decide whether duties will be collected at checkout or demanded when the parcel reaches the customer. Unexpected charges at the door can lead to refused deliveries, complaints and expensive returns.
Where possible, presenting a transparent landed price and using a duties paid service creates a clearer proposition. Customers understand the full cost before purchasing, while retailers retain more control over the delivery experience.
This transparency should extend across product pages, checkout and delivery communications. Hiding the additional cost until the final stage may protect conversion temporarily, but it risks damaging trust. A higher price that is clearly explained is preferable to a lower price that turns out not to be real.
- Improve customs data before increasing automation
Customs performance depends on accurate product descriptions, declared values, commodity codes and country of origin information. Poor data can lead to incorrect duties, delays, inspections and rejected shipments.
This information should form part of the product record and be validated before an item is offered in an international market.
Automation can then apply the data consistently, flagging missing information and identifying shipments likely to encounter problems. 41% of retailers believe AI could help resolve international compliance and tax issues, while 36% see an opportunity to address incorrect shipping data. However, AI cannot compensate for inaccurate underlying information, it will simply process the mistakes faster.
- Redesign returns alongside outbound delivery
Cross-border returns become more problematic when duties increase. Retailers must determine whether charges can be recovered and whether products should be shipped back across the border or consolidated, resold, repaired or disposed of locally.
Returns policies must therefore be considered alongside outbound delivery. Retailers need to understand the full cost and likely recovery value of a return, applying different routes according to product, destination and condition. 23% of large retailers say improving the efficiency and cost of returns is a principal objective for the next 12 months, making it the most frequently selected priority in the research.
- Treat regulatory volatility as permanent
Retailers should not assume the disruption is temporary or that the old economics of low value international ecommerce will return. Customs rules may continue to change, but the direction is towards greater scrutiny, more data and tighter enforcement.
Businesses need operations that can adapt without the need to repeatedly redesign checkout, warehouse and carrier systems. That means maintaining multiple carrier options, keeping customs data accurate, modelling costs continuously and using configurable delivery rules rather than manual decisions.
The end of de minimis means that retailers can no longer treat international delivery as an inexpensive extension of domestic fulfilment. The key to success is understanding costs at order level, positioning inventory intelligently, selecting carriers dynamically and telling customers exactly what they will pay.

items.title: Co-op shuts down standalone on-the-go test stores
items.summary: The Co-op has closed five “micro-stores” where it was trialling a standalone food-to-go offer, but plans to continue offering elements of the concept in existing stores alongside its wider convenience offer Co-op launched the five stand-alone stores during 2025, starting in Solihull, West Midlands, at… This story continues at Co-op shuts down standalone on-the-go test stores Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Co-op launched the five stand-alone stores during 2025, starting in Solihull, West Midlands, at the end of July.
In December it also fitted elements of the concept into a further five existing stores – located in Yorkshire and London – with the ‘on the go’ proposition alongside Co-op’s wider grocery offer.
A co-op spokesperson said: “At Co-op, our food-on-the-go offer is central to our convenience strategy, and we are focussed on driving sustainable growth.
“Our focus was on the fast launch and learn of the proposition and following review of their longer-term viability, we have taken the decision to close our five stand-alone food-on-the-go locations.
“Where the concept works at its best is integrated into our existing stores, alongside our wider grocery offer.
“Where we have retro-fitted the new concept into our existing stores we see strong, successful and sustainable opportunities to further elevate and grow the new proposition, combining breakfast, lunch and dinner on-the-go alongside the convenience of Co-op’s broader grocery range in our existing high foot-traffic locations.
“Our focus moving forward will be on the five retro-fitted sites that we operate and identifying further existing stores where we can integrate elements of the concept.”
The standalone sites were about one-quarter of the size of a typical Co-op convenience store.
At the time of launch, the retailer had hoped to open a further 15 “over the coming months” with a longer-term ambition of reaching several hundred in the next two to three years.
The bespoke store design aimed to cater to ‘on-the-go’ key meal solutions throughout the day, serving up breakfast, lunch and dinner in new formats, from traditional meal deals to the inclusion of hot food served over counter – a first for the Co-op – and a new deli selection offering product innovation “for any time of the day”.
The offer included Costa Coffee, hot baguettes, buttermilk chicken tenders and protein pots, “taking cues from around the world”.
New product development exclusive to the micro-stores was set to include all-day breakfast meal pots, Berry Burst Bircher and Apple & Cinnamon overnight oats.
For lunch, a new deli-selection was to serve offerings such as smoked salmon, egg and spinach pots; sweet potato bhaji wrap; falafel and houmous salad bowls, and tomato, mozzarella and pesto focaccia bagels.
Co-op’s Irresistible pizzas were also available to buy cooked in-store, with shoppers given the option to purchase a hot slice or full pizza.
Opening times were between 7am and 7pm.
